While the use of precomputed scores vastly reduces the computational cost of retrieving SpliceAI predictions, several limitations to their utility have emerged, for which the impact on the prioritisation of likely splice-altering variants in cohort studies has not been established. Methods We identify transcript annotation and genome version inconsistencies impacting the precomputed SpliceAI scores by comparing the original gene annotation file with MANE v1.0 Select transcripts. To quantify the impact that these factors may have in variant prioritisation pipelines for diagnostic purposes, we re-analysed variants in 660 genes linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), identified in 7,221 participants with NDD from the Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project (100kGP). Results We find outdated gene annotations and genome version inconsistencies impact 8.34% of theoretical SNVs included in the SpliceAI precomputed scores, and affect the accuracy of SpliceAI predictions in 34.98% of disease-associated panelApp green genes. In 7,221 Genomics England participants, re-running SpliceAI with updated annotations and parameters results in an increase of 18.2% predicted splice-altering variants compared with variants identified using precomputed scores alone. These variants constitute a diagnostic increase of 11.7% versus the precomputed scores, assessed retrospectively using confirmed diagnoses in 100kGP. To mitigate issues with the precomputed scores we provide ‘SpliceAI-splint’- a command-line tool to allow users to identify variants within a VCF file whose potential splice-altering effects would be missed by the precomputed scores. Conclusions: Although the precomputed scores continue to represent a useful resource in the annotation of variants in cohorts with genetic disorders, we find key limitations that can lead to their missing clinically relevant splice-altering variants, and provide a command-line tool to mitigate these issues.

works.title: Ciprofloxacin resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae: phenotype prediction from genotype and global distribution of resistance determinants
authors: Emília Maria Medeiros de Andrade Belitardo
works.abstract: Abstract Background Ciprofloxacin resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae is common or emerging in many geographies, and knowledge of local resistance rates is important for empirical therapy. While K. pneumoniae ciprofloxacin resistance determinants are known, there is a lack of systematic data on the effect of these determinants, alone and in combination, and there are no publicly accessible tools for predicting ciprofloxacin resistance from whole genome sequence data. Methods The KlebNET-GSP AMR Genotype-Phenotype Group aggregated a matched genotype-phenotype dataset of n = 12,167 K. pneumoniae species complex ( Kp SC) isolates from 27 countries between 2001 and 2021. We developed a rule-based classifier to predict ciprofloxacin resistance by categorizing the number of mutations in the quinolone resistance determining regions of gyrA and parC and the number of plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes, including the presence/absence of aac(6 ' )-Ib-cr (which can acetylate ciprofloxacin). Predictive performance was assessed using the discovery dataset, with the reassessment of discrepant and concordant isolates; and validated using externally contributed datasets ( n = 7,030 Kp SC isolates). Results The rule-based classifier predicted R vs S/I with categorical agreement, sensitivity, and specificity > 96%, and major/very major error rates < 4%. Performance was similar across diverse Kp SC sources (human, animal, other), species, and intra-species lineages. External validation of the classifier yielded overall 90.18% categorical agreement [95% confidence interval (CI), 89.49–90.88%], 8.74% major errors [95% CI, 7.41–10.06%], 4.19% very major errors [95% CI, 3.60–4.77%], and 10.14% minor errors [95% CI, 9.44–10.85%]. We implemented the classifier in Kleborate, a command-line tool that is integrated into the Pathogenwatch web platform. Using this to assess the global distribution of ciprofloxacin resistance determinants in Kp SC genomes available in Pathogenwatch ( n = 31,319, from 109 countries between years 2000–2023), we observed a significant positive association between national quinolone consumption rates and predicted ciprofloxacin resistance (R 2 = 0.20, p = 0.004). Conclusion Ciprofloxacin resistance phenotypes can be reasonably predicted from genotype, which is sufficient for informing surveillance. However, unexplained resistance remains and accuracy is insufficient for clinical applications. We demonstrate the value of aggregating genotype-phenotype data to explore resistance mechanisms and develop predictors, but highlight complexities in combining phenotype data from different assays and standards.

works.title: Germline pathogenic variants identification through comprehensive cancer genome profiling
works.abstract: Comprehensive cancer genome profiling (CGP) is recommended for the identification of actionable somatic mutations in a selected subgroup of cancer patients. Some variants detected by CGP can be constitutional. The aim of this study is to evaluate the rate of potential and confirmed constitutional pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants (overall defined as PVs) identified through CGP according to the recommendations of the European Society of Medical Oncology. This is a prospective interventional trial that enrolled patients with solid cancers in whom molecular assessment was clinically indicated based on national guidelines, referring them for CGP (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06020625). Patients with suspected constitutional variants were subsequently referred for germline testing. The present analysis focuses on the first two years of the program, from January 2022 to December 2023. Of 2688 samples (2674 patients) with a CGP report, more than half were represented by gynecologic cancers (endometrial and ovarian). 16% of the patients were addressed to genetic evaluation for 527 suspected constitutional PVs, with a compliance to genetic counselling of 80%. 331 patients underwent germline testing, of whom 73% harbored at least one PV, with 66% of tested variants confirmed to be germline. Interestingly, 16% of germline variants were secondary findings and 20% of the confirmed “on-tumor” germline PVs were in moderate-risk genes. Twenty additional constitutional PVs were identified in 19 patients based on the results of other somatic tests or through additional tests requested following genetic counselling (0.7% of the entire cohort). Constitutional PVs were detected in about 10% of an unselected solid tumor cohort through CGP. A relevant fraction of the constitutional PVs were secondary findings or constitutional variants in moderate penetrance genes, that would not have been detected based on current guidelines. The integration of CGP with systematic genetic counseling provides a comprehensive approach that optimizes both therapeutic decision-making and identification of hereditary cancer syndromes. Protocol ID: FPG500, ID number: 3837. The study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06020625.

works.title: Comprehensive adjudication identifies 108 high-confidence genetic signals for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
works.abstract: The Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project Gene Verification Committee developed and applied a systematic framework to adjudicate genetic evidence for AD and related dementias, addressing wide variation in association quality. Phase 1 established tiered criteria by evaluating 23 nominated loci across study designs. Phase 2 applied this framework to 29 large-scale genome-wide studies published between January 2015 and September 2022 (date of the last literature search), tiering 163 unique loci. Phase 1 yielded 17 high-confidence association signals, including 12 with specific gene-level support. Phase 2 identified 93 high-confidence single-variant signals and 25 high-confidence variant-set signals. After removal of overlapping signals across evidence classes, a final catalog of 108 unique high-confidence AD/ADRD-associated signals were generated. Prioritized loci highlight APP processing, microglial immunity, and lipid metabolism pathways, including genes not captured by existing resources like Agora or Open Targets. Summarized results can be viewed at https://topgenes.niagads.org/ . This rigorously adjudicated catalog represents the most comprehensive AD/ADRD genetics resource to date, providing a foundation for functional validation and therapeutic discovery with broad applicability to complex diseases.

works.title: Resolving disease causality by integrating polygenic risk into propensity score matching
works.abstract: Disentangling causal relationships between diseases from associations driven by shared genetic and environmental risk remains a major challenge. We developed PRIMA (polygenic risk–integrated matching approach), a framework that incorporates exposure-specific polygenic risk scores and clinical covariates into propensity score matching. We evaluated PRIMA using liability-threshold simulations and disease-pair analyses in 333,370 unrelated UK Biobank participants of European ancestry, and compared its estimates with clinical matching, Mendelian randomization and survival analyses. In simulations, PRIMA reduced bias due to shared genetic liability and recovered effect estimates closer to the expected causal effects than clinical matching alone, while remaining sensitive to unmeasured confounding. In UK Biobank analyses, integrating polygenic risk improved genetic and clinical balance and materially altered association estimates for a subset of disease pairs. PRIMA identified additional associations not detected by Mendelian randomization and showed greater concordance with survival analyses. PRIMA provides a scalable framework for incorporating polygenic liability into observational disease-pair analyses. It complements existing causal inference methods, although causal interpretation remains conditional on appropriate model specification, sufficient overlap and adequate control of confounding.

works.title: Tracing the origins of multidrug resistant bacteria in Ukraine
works.abstract: Abstract Background A key medical characteristic of the current conflict in Ukraine has been the extraordinary number of wounds being infected by multidrug resistant organisms (MDROs). The origin and spread of these organisms have been the subject of intense interest and debate, yet the reservoirs and transmission routes remain poorly defined. In this study, environmental sampling was performed across the Ukrainian medical evacuation chain to better understand transmission dynamics. Methods 127 environmental swabs were collected from environmental surfaces in three frontline hospitals ( n = 17 swabs), two evacuation assets (12 swabs), a large regional healthcare facility that provides full clinical and surgical capabilities (23 swabs), and three definitive care and rehabilitative hospitals (75 swabs). Swabs were incubated in Brain Heart Infusion broth and then cultured on non-selective and selective agars. Short- and long-read sequencing were performed using an Illumina NextSeq 2000 and MinION, respectively. The resulting genomes were compared to a collection of clinical bacteria cultured from patients in healthcare facilities in Denmark, Germany, The Netherlands, and Ukraine. Results Bacterial growth was recorded from 112 swabs (88%) and 280 distinct environmental strains, representing 89 bacterial species, were cultured. Notably, MDROs were effectively absent from the frontline facilitates and evacuation assets but were detected in 48–56% of environmental samples from rear-echelon hospitals. Genomic analysis revealed that these rear-echelon hospital environments were dominated by epidemic lineages of Acinetobacter baumannii , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , and Klebsiella pneumoniae that frequently carried carbapenemases. A genetic comparison of the environmental bacteria with clinical strains cultured from injured soldiers and refugees receiving care in hospitals in Ukraine, Denmark, Germany, and The Netherlands revealed high levels of genetic relatedness. Compounding the problem, plasmidome analysis identified horizontal dissemination of resistance genes across species within the hospital environment. Conclusions These findings implicate hospital environments as key reservoirs and amplifiers of MDROs during conflict, highlighting their central role in sustaining local transmission and international spread.

works.title: Evaluating gene expression-based approaches for functional assessment of non-coding variants in neurodevelopmental disorders
works.abstract: Non-coding variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders are difficult to interpret because their regulatory effects are subtle and depend on locus- and stage-specific epigenetic contexts. Transcriptional mis-regulation of nearby genes is the most reliable sign of functional relevance. RNA-seq studies usually detect this via differential gene expression (DEG) analysis, which requires healthy controls and typically more than twofold expression changes. Allele-specific expression (ASE) analysis, may detect subtler effects by directly comparing expression of alleles on the intact and the affected chromosomes within the same sample. We evaluated ASE power using real RNA-seq data, in silico simulations, and a clinical case. We combined transcriptome profiling of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and neural progenitor cells (NPCs) with in silico modeling of gene-expression changes to estimate statistical power. We compared two strategies: DEG between variant carriers and non-carriers, and ASE within heterozygous individuals. For clinical validation, we used CRISPR-Cas9 base editing to introduce a synonymous single-nucleotide variant (SNV) adjacent to the candidate regulatory variant in patient-derived NPCs and performed targeted RNA-seq. Simulations and empirical data showed that DEG has higher power for most genes, even with substantial inter-individual or biological variability. ASE surpassed DEG only for genes containing heterozygous SNVs and sequenced at high depth. In a patient carrying a translocation breakpoint near AUTS2 , we generated iPSC and NPC lines with SNV-labeled AUTS2 alleles and devised an inexpensive target-enrichment assay for high-sensitivity ASE profiling, but neither approach detected gene misregulation consistent with the phenotype under current biological models. Our results suggested that DEG and ASE assays are complementary rather than competing strategies. We also demonstrate a practical path to sensitive ASE detection, both in whole-transcriptome and targeted RNA-sequencing, using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated allele labeling. This framework helps researchers to choose cost-effective transcriptomic designs for the functional validation of non-coding variants implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.

works.title: Pilot Evaluation of Saliva Samples as An Alternative to Blood for Large-scale Whole-genome Sequencing Studies
works.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) studies have traditionally relied on blood as the primary DNA source and manual workflows. As population-based genomics studies expand, minimally invasive and easily deployable biospecimen collection methods compatible with high-throughput automation are increasingly needed. In this pilot study, we established a real-world, end-to-end automated WGS workflow, encompassing robotic DNA extraction, library preparation, sequencing and quality control. We compared saliva- and blood-derived WGS across key analytical parameters, including performance at each step of the workflow, overall cost, and feasibility for future large-scale implementation. First, germline variant calls from saliva and blood samples showed high concordance, reaching 97% genome-wide and over 99% in high-confidence genomic regions. Second, key workflow metrics, including DNA quality and sequencing quality, were comparable between saliva and blood samples, while saliva samples had a lower per-sample cost. We compared three commercially available saliva collection kits and found that all achieved at least 95% genome-wide concordance with matched blood samples, with differences primarily driven by cost. Finally, automated saliva processing produced sequencing and short variant calling metrics broadly comparable to manual processing in a small paired comparison. Collectively, these results provide a practical and scalable solution for incorporating saliva into future large cohort sequencing studies. Larger and more diverse studies are needed to further validate the robustness and generalizability of this pilot study.

works.title: CDH1 loss remodels gene expression and lineage identity in human mammary epithelial cells
works.abstract: Invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is a common subtype of breast cancer, molecularly defined by genetic loss of CDH1, and subsequent loss of cell adhesion protein E-cadherin, in ~95% of ILC. Though CDH1 loss occurs early in ILC oncogenesis, it is unclear how this facilitates transformation. We modeled early CDH1 loss using "normal" human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC), i.e., finite lifespan cells reflecting early hyperplasia, and targeted E-cadherin signaling using antibodies versus causing genetic CDH1 loss using siRNA or CRISPR/Cas9-knockout. Transcriptome analysis across four HMEC models showed that the mode of E-cadherin targeting is critical for the subsequent phenotype. Antibody-mediated inhibition of cell-cell contacts induced gene signatures of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), consistent with the role of E-cadherin suppression during the EMT process. Conversely, genetic CDH1 loss - as in ILC oncogenesis - repressed EMT signatures, and instead remodeled gene expression toward a luminal epithelial phenotype. RNA-seq, single cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, microscopy, and ATAC-seq analyses support that CDH1 loss induces lineage remodeling to a luminal state, which is mirrored in transcriptomic analysis of clinical ILC precursor lesions. By isolating luminal versus basal cells prior to CDH1 knockout, we found that CDH1 loss led to remodeling of lineage identity in both populations, converging on a new lineage homeostasis with a luminal progenitor-like phenotype. Consistent with the shift to a luminal progenitor phenotype, CDH1 loss enhanced proliferative capacity over the finite lifespan of the HMECs, highlighting a feature of early CDH1 loss that may contribute to clonal advantage during tumor initiation. Moreover, CDH1 loss enhanced anoikis resistance, a defining feature of ILC cells. Our findings support that genetic loss of CDH1 in mammary epithelial cells induces transcriptional and phenotypic changes consistent with lineage identity remodeling toward a luminal progenitor-like state, which may underpin the mechanism by which early CDH1 loss mediates ILC oncogenesis.

works.title: The peculiar properties of pericentromeric regions of genomes and their influence on sex chromosome evolution
works.abstract: Results from recent genome sequences support the idea that the lack of recombination across extensive sex-linked regions (SLRs) in some species may be a pre-existing feature, due mainly to the sex-determining locus being located near a centromere. This would cause it to be affected by the "centromere-effect", which ensures low recombination rates near centromeres. In such cases, it is unnecessary to invoke any active recombination suppression process, or to debate ideas about the types of selection involved. In this review, I outline the properties of genome regions that recombine rarely, including pericentromeric regions of chromosomes, and discuss SLRs that overlap with pericentromeric regions. Unsurprisingly, it is difficult to distinguish special features of such SLRs that would suggest they have undergone a recombination suppression process. The property most likely to be specific to completely SLRs is major gene loss from Y- or W-linked regions of genes found in their respective X- or Z-linked counterparts, and this asymmetry is observed in many species. However, if pericentromeric regions are characterised by ephemeral gene content and low gene expression, asymmetry between pericentromeric SLRs might be less pronounced than in SLRs in other genome regions, and similar Y and X degeneration levels are indeed documented in several species. Additionally, some such SLRs may not be completely sex-linked, which could explain findings of extensive SLRs with low Y-X (or W-Z) divergence.

works.title: Germline dependence in protein language model retrieval of adaptive immune receptors
works.abstract: Abstract Protein language models (PLMs) are increasingly used to represent adaptive immune receptors, yet their advantage over classical sequence comparison remains unclear. We benchmarked general and receptor-specific PLMs against classical sequence-comparison methods for antigen-specific nearest-neighbor retrieval across four B- and T-cell receptor databases. Using CDR3 sequences alone, classical methods consistently outperformed general PLMs: BLOSUM62 and Levenshtein exceeded ESM2 variants by 7–12 percentage points in retrieval accuracy. Among receptor-specific models, only SCEPTR and, on one database, TCR2vec matched these baselines, although both additionally encoded V-gene information. AntiBERTa2 and IgBert did not close the performance gap. Using full variable-domain sequences, alignment and PLM performance converged. Germline-reversion, region-masking, and V-gene control analyses indicated that this convergence largely reflected conserved germline-derived context, particularly V-gene identity, with limited evidence for improved extraction of antigen-specific information from the CDRs. Germline dependence also extended to SCEPTR and TCR2vec. Heavily mutated HIV-1 antibodies provided a setting-specific exception to this pattern. Random train-test splits yielded retrieval accuracy 15–28 percentage points higher than clone-aware splits, consistent with optimistic performance estimates due to clonal leakage. These findings emphasize the need for strong sequence-comparison baselines and explicit germline controls when evaluating immune-receptor representations and support clone-aware splitting as a minimum benchmark standard.

works.title: Continuous mass photometry by single-molecule trapping
works.abstract: The dynamic choreography of biomolecular interactions underpins the processes of life, but its direct observation remains challenging. Here we introduce continuous mass photometry, enabling hour-long, mass-resolved observation of individual biomolecules tethered to supported lipid bilayers, their complexes and interactions, with up to sub-kilodalton mass precision and millisecond temporal resolution. Our approach represents a quantitative time-resolved single-molecule measurement modality for studying complex biomolecular mechanisms in action.

works.title: Sequence design for three-dimensional genome folding using Akita Semifreddo
works.abstract: DNA sequence directs genome folding, which in turn shapes enhancer-promoter communication and gene expression. How to design DNA sequences that produce desired folding patterns remains largely unexplored. Here we present Akita Semifreddo, which combines an efficient "half-frozen" version of the AkitaV2 genome folding model with the Ledidi sequence optimizer to design DNA sequences with desired folding in silico. We demonstrate that this framework enables design for major folding features – boundaries, dots, and flames – with desired positions and strengths. In short, Akita Semifreddo provides a platform for dissecting the sequence grammar of genome folding and engineering synthetic regulatory landscapes.

works.title: ReadsRatio: a facile method for cell type deconvolution with cross-platform applications
works.abstract: Existing methylation-based cfDNA deconvolution methods are sensitive to sequencing depth, reference quality, and platform variability. We develope ReadsRatio, an approach to estimate tissue proportions using the ratio of unmethylated reads within cell type-specific marker regions, without requiring reference methylation intensity signals. Compared to conventional methods, ReadsRatio detects specific tissue involvement in both simulations and clinical cohorts involving lupus, kidney transplantation, and COVID-19. It maintains accuracy across sequencing platforms and at reduced sequencing depths, enabling substantial cost savings in our preliminary estimations. ReadsRatio provides a versatile, cost-efficient framework for cfDNA deconvolution with broad research and clinical applicability.

works.title: Urbanisation drives parallel genomic divergence across cities and bumble bee species
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Urbanisation imposes pervasive environmental change, yet it remains unclear whether evolutionary responses to cities are largely idiosyncratic or whether similar selective pressures across cities repeatedly generate predictable genomic outcomes. RESULTS: Here, we analyse whole-genome data from 524 individuals of three widespread bumble bee species sampled across nine independent urban-rural pairs in Central Europe to test whether urban environments drive parallel evolutionary responses across cities and species. Genetic diversity responded idiosyncratically to urbanisation, with two species showing no detectable urban-rural differences and one species exhibiting reduced diversity in cities, consistent with species-specific ecological traits and habitat requirements. Despite weak population structure and high gene flow in all species, we detected consistent and replicated genomic divergence associated with urban environments. Genome-environment association analyses revealed parallel allele-frequency shifts at the same loci across independent cities for each species, while selective sweep scans identified repeated signals of positive selection in urban populations. Across species, urban-associated divergence was highly polygenic and occurred predominantly in non-coding regions with potential regulatory roles. Although the specific genes involved were largely species-specific, functional enrichment analyses revealed strong convergence across species, particularly in pathways related to physiological stress responses, neurocognitive and behavioural processes, metabolism and immunity. CONCLUSIONS: Together, these results suggest that urban environments can impose recurrent selective pressures, generating predictable and parallel genomic responses across cities and species despite ongoing gene flow. More broadly, our findings highlight polygenic, potentially regulatory adaptation as an important component of evolutionary responses to urban environments.

works.title: Mitonuclear control of transcription complexes regulates tRNA splicing
works.abstract: The human genome has hundreds of tRNA genes, a subset of which is intervened by short introns. Transcription of the latter genes by RNA polymerase (Pol) III generates precursor tRNAs that undergo splicing by the tRNA splicing complex, in addition to the removal of flanking sequences by RNase P and RNase Z. The former enzyme consists of tRNA splicing endoribonuclease complex and tRNA ligase complex. However, it was unknown how and where the human tRNA splicing complex executes its function in cells. We show that transcription complexes assembled on intron-containing tRNA genes possess a tRNA ligase complex and that this enzyme is regulated by a mitonuclear communication mechanism. A cytoplasmic, mitochondria-associated HSPC117, the catalytic subunit of the tRNA ligase complex, transiently relocates to the nucleoplasm in the S phase of the cell cycle to promote the second step of splicing, exon ligation, of select tRNAs. This nuclear localized RTCB-type ligase acts as an integral part of transcription complexes. Knockout of HSPC117 or expression of an inactive mutant of this enzyme leads to severe inhibition of transcription and exon ligation due to the assembly of deficient transcription complexes. Inhibition also brings to deficiency of the perinucleolar compartments, as a result of reduced expression of the H1 RNA essential to Pol III transcription in cells. This study demonstrates that transcription complexes execute splicing of select intron-containing tRNAs and that this two-stage reaction is time-based on a mitonuclear communication mechanism that controls the tRNA ligase HSPC117 in human cells.

works.title: Integration-free and cluster-free detection of localized differential gene coexpression in single-cell data with DiCoLo
works.abstract: Detecting changes in gene coordination patterns between biological conditions and identifying the cell populations in which these changes occur are key challenges in single-cell analysis. Existing approaches often compare gene co-expression between predefined cell clusters or rely on aligning cells across conditions. These strategies can be suboptimal when changes occur within small subpopulations or when batch effects obscure the underlying biological signal. To address these challenges, we introduce DiCoLo, a framework that identifies genes exhibiting differential co-localization, defined as changes in coordinated expression within localized cell neighborhoods -subsets of highly similar cells in the transcriptomic space. Importantly, DiCoLo does not rely on cell clustering or cross-condition alignment. For each condition, DiCoLo constructs a gene graph using Optimal Transport distances that reflect gene co-localization patterns across the cell manifold. Then, it identifies differential gene programs by detecting changes in connectivity patterns between the gene graphs. We show that DiCoLo robustly identifies differential gene co-localization even under weak signals or complex batch effects, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmark datasets. When applied to mouse hair follicle development data, DiCoLo reveals coordinated gene programs and emerging cell populations driven by perturbations in morphogen signaling that underlie dermal condensate differentiation. Overall, these results establish DiCoLo as a powerful framework for uncovering localized differential transcriptional coordinated patterns in single-cell data.

works.title: Chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation of Octodon degus
works.abstract: Abstract High-quality reference genomes are essential for comparative and functional genomics yet remain unavailable for many emerging model organisms. Here, we report OctDeg2.0, a chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the degu ( Octodon degus), generated using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C scaffolding from a single male individual. Octodon degus is of growing interest as a natural animal model for aging and Alzheimer’s disease research. The 3.4 billion base-pair assembly comprises 28 autosomes and both sex chromosomes, with markedly improved contiguity and completeness over the prior short-read assembly while maintaining high base accuracy. The new assembly provides substantially enhanced gene annotation, clearer resolution of chromatin architecture and cis-regulatory element landscapes, with much improved characterization of repetitive and structurally complex regions, including centromeres and segmental duplications. We present a streamlined and reproducible pipeline for high-resolution de novo genome assembly and gene annotation applicable to other emerging model organisms. This work establishes a robust genomic resource for studying molecular and cellular mechanisms in health and disease in Octodon degus .

works.title: An integrative computational approach for obstacle avoidance during action selection
works.abstract: Action selection in cluttered environments, where individuals must simultaneously pursue goals and avoid obstacles, presents a significant challenge for the brain. To understand the underlying mechanisms of action selection in such contexts, we propose a computational model that extends stochastic optimal control theory through a novel framework for obstacle avoidance. The model decomposes action selection into a weighted combination of individual control policies, each generated for either target approach or obstacle avoidance. By integrating value information from goals, obstacles, and actions into a unified measure of “relative desirability”, the model dynamically determines the contribution of each policy to the overall action selection process. We evaluated the framework using simulated target-reaching tasks in cluttered environments based on previous human studies. The results showed that the model qualitatively captures key features of human motor behavior, including the influence of obstacle properties on movement trajectories and the transient tendency to initiate movements toward obstacles before avoidance. This work offers new insights into the dynamic interaction between approach and avoidance behaviors, providing a basis for future studies of action selection in more complex and naturalistic settings.

works.title: Calsequestrin localization at RyR2 clusters enables calcium wave propagation in ventricular myocytes
works.abstract: Intracellular calcium waves in cardiac myocytes propagate through a fire-diffuse-fire mechanism in which calcium released from one RyR2 cluster diffuses to neighboring clusters and triggers their activation. Yet propagation faces a fundamental physical difficulty: the calcium signal must cross distances of 1–2 μ m between Z-planes while being attenuated by cytosolic buffering and diffusion, and at the same time the release site depletes its local sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium store. How waves propagate efficiently despite these constraints has remained unclear. We developed a three-dimensional computational model of mouse ventricular myocytes at submicrometer resolution to address this question. Our central finding is that co-localization of calsequestrin2 (CASQ2) with RyR2 clusters is required for robust wave propagation. In a physiological model, where CASQ2 is concentrated at release sites as observed experimentally, calcium waves propagate reliably across the cell with velocities that match the experimental range. In contrast, when CASQ2 is distributed uniformly throughout the sarcoplasmic reticulum, keeping total CASQ2 unchanged, the wavefront stalls. These results identify CASQ2–RyR2 co-localization as a key structural requirement for effective calcium wave propagation in ventricular myocytes.

works.title: Rapid and Reliable Structural Modeling of Adaptive Immune Receptors Using an Optimized AlphaFold3 workflow
works.abstract: AlphaFold (AF), a deep-learning based protein modelling approach, has revolutionized structural biology by generally achieving near-experimental accuracy in protein structure prediction.An impactful application of AF is the modelling of antibodies (Abs) and T-cell receptors (TCRs), key mediators of cellular immunity, whose structural specificity underlies responses in cancer, infection, and autoimmune diseases.In this work, we analyse AF3 performance by systematically examining how MSA composition, number of inference phases and inference parameters affect prediction accuracy and computational efficiency.We present an acceleration of ~45-fold of the AF3 MSA phase using reduced UniRef90 subsets, combined with up to a 3.6-fold increase in AF3 inference speed through optimized parameters.We provide a highly accurate variant of the AF3 workflow specifically optimized for the modelling of the Abs and TCRs receptor domains, enabling rapid, reliable structural predictions at a scale suitable for high-throughput immunological studies.Our findings provide a foundation for faster therapeutic discovery and deeper molecular mechanism understanding of immune recognition.Teaser: By improving key steps in the process, we made AlphaFold3 ~45 times faster in the multiple sequence alignment stage at modeling specific immune proteins Downloaded from https://spj.science.org

works.title: ECbiomarker: A Clinically Annotated Knowledge Base of Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Treatment-related Biomarkers in Endometrial Cancer
works.abstract: Background: Endometrial cancer (EC) is a heterogeneous malignancy for which biomarker evidence is distributed across studies using different assays, endpoints, and patient populations.Objectives: To compile a literature-curated knowledge base of reported EC biomarkers that supports evidence navigation and research on diagnostic, prognostic, and treatment-related biomarkers.Methods: PubMed was searched with a MeSH-based query restricted to publications dated from January 1, 1975, to July 1, 2023, and eligible studies were manually curated.Curated records were annotated with external bioinformatics and genomic resources.The database was implemented with MySQL and a Python-based (Flask) web framework.Results: Audit of the v1.0 master basic table identified 1,103 database records associated with 635 distinct PMIDs.After trimming leading and trailing whitespace, 617 distinct biomarker-name strings were identified; case-insensitive counting yielded 603 strings.Synonyms were not merged.Application labels comprised 382 diagnostic, 579 prognostic, and 139 treatment-related records, with three records carrying missing or invalid application labels.The resource preserves study-specific cutoffs and effect directions rather than harmonizing or pooling them.Downloaded from https://spj.science.orgon October 27, 2026 Conclusion: ECbiomarker is a literature-curated, disease-specific repository of EC biomarker records.This resource supports evidence navigation and biomarker research in endometrial cancer.

works.title: A Proof-of-Concept Computational Workflow for Model-Based Estimation of Temporomandibular Joint Loading During Mandibular Movement Using a Kinematics-Driven Generic Musculoskeletal Model
works.abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) biomechanics are difficult to assess in vivo because mandibular motion, muscle recruitment, occlusion, and neuromuscular control interact dynamically.This proof-of-concept study examined whether participant-specific mandibular kinematics obtained by three-dimensional motion capture could drive a generic mandible/TMJ musculoskeletal model in inverse dynamics and whether model-derived masseter waveforms could be compared exploratorily with masseter-region surface electromyography (sEMG).Five young adult women without self-reported temporomandibular disorder history or current symptoms performed maximum opening, self-estimated submaximal opening, lateral excursion, and protrusion-retrusion using customized mouthpieces for jaw tracking.Kinematic data were acquired from all participants.Inverse-dynamics outputs were obtained for P1, P2, P4, and P5; P3 failed because of a model error.Because P2, P4, and P5 showed frequent force spikes, detailed force analysis was limited to P1. Retrospective CORrelation and Analysis (CORA) comparisons of bilateral sEMG and stored model-derived masseter signals yielded mean scores of 0.6009 in P1 and 0.6406 across 24 comparisons in four participants.However, incomplete records of signal construction, scaling, trial handling, and CORA settings precluded reproducible verification.In P1, the right TMJ was treated as the primary output because marker registration produced left-sided muscle overactivation in the unscaled generic model.Mean right-TMJ resultant force during submaximal opening was 79.11 N. The superior lateral pterygoid showed the largest predicted relative force contribution, but this remains a modelgenerated hypothesis without sensitivity analysis.The workflow demonstrated case-level technical executability but not cross-participant robustness, physiological validity, or clinical utility.Larger studies using anatomically personalized models and patient cohorts are therefore required.

works.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
works.abstract: A central challenge in immunology and therapeutic design is accurately predicting the diverse interactions between T cell receptors and peptide-human leukocyte antigen (pHLA) complexes. Existing machine learning tools are hindered by incomplete sequence data and biased nonbinding examples. Here we present Hi-TPH, a large-scale hierarchical dataset featuring an on-the-fly selection method for generating nonbinding data. We further develop Hi-TPH-PLMs, a collection of protein language models (PLMs) with varied architectures and scales, fine-tuned on Hi-TPH. These models achieve a 19.2% performance gain over state-of-the-art tools on an external wet-lab test set. Leveraging the hierarchical structure of Hi-TPH, detailed analyses dissect the contribution of different molecular components to binding prediction and reveal their synergistic interplay; for instance, the prediction contribution of HLA relies on the presence of full T cell receptor chains. Hi-TPH and Hi-TPH-PLMs are publicly released to support the development of more reliable tools for advanced immunoinformatics research and personalized immunotherapy.

works.title: Quantification method affects replicability of eQTL analysis, colocalization and TWAS
Interferon-α directs hematopoietic stem cells toward competing fates
fastGxE is a powerful method for uncovering genotype–environment interactions in biobanks
Distinct core minor pilin complexes prime specialized type IV filaments in cyanobacteria
works.abstract: The model cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 encodes, in addition to the major pilin of the Type IV pilus filament, an extensive, partially uncharacterized repertoire of minor pilins. For those cyanobacterial minor pilins that have been characterized, their roles span a surprisingly diverse range of functions. To elucidate the roles of uncharacterized minor pilins in a systematic way, we applied structural phylogenomics across 90 genomes, classifying cyanobacterial pilins into six conserved families that form two distinct putative core priming complexes. We demonstrate that these complexes initiate the assembly of two morphologically distinct Type IV pilus filaments: short, hyper-dynamic pili for natural competence, and long, adhesive pili for motility and phototaxis. Structural analysis revealed a conserved β-solenoid domain in PilX subunits, which we propose fulfills the capping function of PilY1 homologs. Proteomic data indicate that the minor pilin PilX2 facilitates the assembly of motility pili, which is required to maintain DnaJ3 co-chaperone levels and trigger cAMP-dependent surface sensing. These findings challenge the concept of a single multipurpose pilus, establishing that cyanobacteria utilize a shared machinery to assemble two specialized filaments, each primed by distinct core minor pilin complexes to meet the conflicting biophysical requirements of DNA uptake and surface motility.

works.title: Extensive mobilome heterogeneity in a widespread endosymbiont: A candidate dimeric plasmid and highly fragmented prophages in Wolbachia from Culex pipiens
works.abstract: The obligate, intracellular bacteria Wolbachia have gained increasing interest due to their selfish modifications of host arthropod reproduction, impacts on host evolution, and utility in vector control efforts to reduce arbovirus transmission worldwide. Despite their highly reduced genomes, Wolbachia harbor a rich mobilome that includes phages, insertion sequences and plasmids in mosquito vectors. However, these repeat-rich mobile genetic elements are notoriously difficult to assemble and can generate artificial, chimeric sequences that obscure their true diversity. As a result, conventional genome sequencing and assembly approaches often fail to resolve the complexity, leaving critical gaps of knowledge on how these elements evolve, mobilize, and shape both symbiont and host genomes. To address these challenges, we established a novel Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing strategy that avoids prior PCR amplification and leverages single-dissected, female ovaries. Using this approach, we report and characterize-directly from native long-read molecules-the first near-complete Wolbachia genome and its mobile elements from individual ovaries of the mosquito vector Culex pipiens molestus. Additional short reads from individuals of the same strain were used to assess and validate candidate mutations, particularly in repetitive regions. We report a new dimeric structure of the pWCP plasmid, suggesting the existence of multimeric plasmid forms potentially associated with active replication. We also observed extensive fragmentation of prophage WO regions despite long read sequencing, underscoring their structural complexity. Raw long read analyses recovered multiple alternative gene syntenies within WO regions, pointing to heterogeneous prophage architectures missed by the assembly and marked diversity of WO elements in Wolbachia of Culex pipiens (wPip) group strains. Taken together, our results illuminate the structural heterogeneity of the endosymbiont genome that is shaped by integrated and episomal mobile elements.

works.title: Auxilin in enteroendocrine cells controls intestinal homeostasis through inter-cell signaling relays
works.abstract: Adult stem cells are critical for the homeostasis of residential tissue and organism fitness. Residential stem cells must constantly perceive external and internal signals and adjust their proliferation rate accordingly to avoid unlimited proliferation or premature differentiation. However, how differentiated cells affect stem cell proliferation and tissue homeostasis through cell-cell communication still remains poorly understood. Here, we unveil an unprecedented function of Auxilin (Aux) in enteroendocrine cells (EEs) by restricting intestinal stem cell (ISC) proliferation. aux depletion in all EEs leads to intestinal homeostasis disruption. The levels of Slit are dramatically reduced in aux-depleted EEs and cytokine Upd3 expression is significantly increased in some aux-depleted EEs and neighboring wild type enterocytes (ECs). Ectopic expression of slit could effectively rescue the defects observed in prosts > auxRNAi intestines. Interestingly, EGFR signaling is ectopically activated due to EGFR accumulation in aux-depleted EEs. Further inhibiting EGFR signaling completely suppresses the defects in prosts > auxRNAi intestines. Finally, EGFR signaling suppresses slit transcription by Pointed binding to slit regulatory regions. Together, these data show that Aux in EEs restrains ISCs from excessive proliferation and aberrant progeny differentiation to maintain intestinal homeostasis through inter-cell communications. Thus our study uncovers the underlying mechanism of how stem cell proliferation is properly controlled by differentiated cells through inter-cell signaling relays during tissue homeostasis and tumorigenesis.

works.title: Transcriptome-based, genome-scale metabolic modelling of Haemonchus contortus during development and between sexes
TERP: Machine Learning-based prediction of TCR-peptide binding specificity
works.abstract: Abstract Motivation The ability to accurately predict TCR-pMHC binding is crucial for the development of cancer immunotherapies, diagnostics, and new vaccines. Tetramer-based single-cell TCR sequencing techniques have provided information on TCR clonotypes and their cognate peptide antigens, which have been catalogued in databases such as VDJdb, IEDB, and McPAS-TCR. Recent advances in AI/ML techniques have opened up the opportunities for development of machine learning based methods for accurate predictions of TCR-pMHC binding. Results We have developed TERP (TCR-Epitope Recognition Prediction) based on a systematic analysis using different types of embeddings for CDR3β sequences of TCRs and putative peptide antigens, and a variety of different machine learning methods like CNN, ANN, random forest, XGBoost, logistic regression and naïve Bayes etc. Extensive benchmarking studies using different types of negative datasets (naïve TCRs and random non-cognate pairing) and different splits for test datasets revealed that the Random Forest algorithm and BLOSUM50 features have best predictive performance. TERP had superior performance compared to other published methods for TCR-Split (80:20 random split) and Strict-Split (less frequent peptide-TCR pairs in the test set) settings in both naïve and cross-combination negative sampling. Further, TERP demonstrated generalizability in predicting unseen TCR-peptide pairs, whereas other models failed to do so. TERP has also been implemented as a user-friendly web portal, accessible at http://www.nii.ac.in/TERP. The portal offers various functionalities, including TCR-peptide binding prediction, screening of TCRs for a given epitope, and prediction of epitopes for TCR clonotypes using CDR3β sequences or results from TCRSeq in 10x or immunoseq format. Availability and implementation Freely available online at http://www.nii.ac.in/TERP. The website is developed with the Django Python framework and supports all major browsers.

works.title: GBZ-base and GAF-base: Indexed pangenome file formats
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: Existing pangenome file formats are designed for batch processing. Graphs must be loaded into memory, and alignment files must be read sequentially. Indexed file formats that can be used directly from disk would be more appropriate for interactive applications. RESULTS: We propose GBZ-base and GAF-base - SQLite-backed file formats comparable to GBZ and GAF. GBZ-base supports efficient extraction of local subgraphs, and GAF-base lets us extract all alignments to the subgraph. Additionally, GAF-base is smaller than any other file format for sequence-to-graph alignments. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: From https://github.com/jltsiren/gbz-base and https://crates.io/crates/gbz-base under the MIT license.

works.title: SomatiX: accurate and efficient somatic SNV detection from matched tumor-normal long-read DNA sequencing
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: Accurate somatic single-nucleotide variant (SNV) calling from matched tumor-normal long-read DNA sequencing remains challenging because sequencing errors, variable tumor purity, tumor-in-normal contamination, and low variant allele fractions (VAFs) can obscure tumor-specific signals. Although recent deep-learning methods have improved long-read somatic variant calling, robust low-VAF detection and efficient genome-scale analysis remain important methodological challenges. RESULTS: We present SomatiX, a deep-learning method for somatic SNV detection from matched tumor-normal long-read DNA sequencing data, built on an allele-aware pileup representation. In comprehensive cancer benchmark analyses across diverse cell-line datasets, sequencing contexts, VAF bins, and minimum variant-supporting read thresholds, SomatiX outperformed DeepSomatic and ClairS in F1 score across most Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) benchmark conditions and achieved competitive performance on Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) data. Across the held-out chromosome 1 cancer cell-line benchmarks, at the threshold of ≥3 variant-supporting reads and a VAF ≥0.05, SomatiX achieved mean F1 scores of 0.986 for ONT data and 0.988 for PacBio data. SomatiX showed particularly strong performance for low-VAF SNVs in ONT data while using a compact model and achieving the fastest runtime among the evaluated tools. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: SomatiX is available at https://github.com/colinliuzelin/SomatiX and archived at Zenodo under DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22062438. The repository includes source code, trained models, and benchmarking scripts.

works.title: Ernie-Switcher: RNA foundation model-guided design of programmable RNA devices in a navigable landscape
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: Recent advances in biological foundation models have enabled new opportunities for data-driven molecular engineering. However, designing programmable RNA devices remains challenging because of the vast, nonlinear sequence-structure-function landscape. Here, we present Ernie-Switcher, a deep learning framework built upon the RNA foundation model (RNAErnie), comprising three coupled components: (i) integration of RNAErnie-derived sequence-phenotype representations for realistic design generation and filtering, (ii) characterization of RNA landscape navigability as a theoretical basis for sequence optimization, and (iii) incorporation of biophysical constraints to maintain optimization trajectories within biologically plausible bounds. RESULTS: We validated Ernie-Switcher using RNA toehold switches. Theoretically, the observed lower bound on threshold navigability (86.4%) of the RNA landscape supports the theoretical feasibility of RNA switch sequence optimization. Experimentally, the optimized toehold switches achieved ON/OFF expression ratios of up to 35-fold in Escherichia coli. Collectively, RNAErnie-guided sequence optimization provides a scalable strategy for engineering high-performance RNA devices. To facilitate broad adoption, we deployed Ernie-Switcher as a freely accessible web platform. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The Python code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/zhutiblah/Ernie-Switcher and are archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21859277. The RNA toehold switch design platform is available at https://ernie-switcher.bioinformatics-syn.org/.

works.title: Multi-view state-space modeling for zero-shot circRNA–miRNA interaction prediction
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: CircRNA-miRNA interactions (CMIs) play regulatory roles in human diseases and provide clues for therapeutic target discovery. However, most existing prediction methods rely on circRNA-miRNA pairs and overlook disease-level regulatory contexts, which limits their ability to characterize cross-pathway dependencies in zero-shot inference. RESULTS: We propose MV-S2M, a multi-view state-space modeling framework that integrates molecular attributes to enhance relational reasoning, enabling zero-shot CMI prediction. Specifically, MV-S2M performs structure-aware diffusion to enrich molecular priors and constructs disease-mediated semantic subgraphs. It then incorporates state-space modeling to capture long-range dependencies and view-specific regulatory patterns. The learned multi-view representations are fused through a linear projection and fed into an MLP for CMI prediction. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MV-S2M achieves state-of-the-art performance under both zero-shot and conventional settings. Cold-start evaluations reveal distinct generalization behavior across different unseen-entity settings. Case studies illustrate the contribution of meta-path-guided semantic subgraphs to CMI prediction. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/591286260/MV and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22858403.

works.title: IsoPrism predicts isoform usage from short-read transcriptomes through structure-guided competitive allocation
works.abstract: Short-read (SR) single-cell and spatial transcriptomics characterize gene expression but provide limited resolution of within-gene isoform usage. Here we present IsoPrism, a structure-guided competitive allocation framework that predicts isoform proportions from gene-level expression. IsoPrism combines individual expression and local expression context with transcript structural annotations, using shared iterative updates to preserve non-negative, gene-normalized proportions. Joint supervision from individual long-read (LR) counts and group-level isoform usage enables prediction in samples without matched LR measurements. Across five transfer scenarios derived from three paired transcriptomic resources, IsoPrism achieved the highest mean dominant isoform accuracy, compositional similarity, and cluster-level allocation correlation among eight evaluated methods. Ablation analyses supported complementary contributions from structural queries, expression context, iterative allocation, and dual-resolution supervision. Applied to a developing mouse cortex atlas, IsoPrism identified stage- and cell-type-associated isoform-usage patterns, including variation in the predicted relative usage of two Pkm transcripts. IsoPrism enables isoform-usage analysis of SR transcriptomes by transferring information from paired LR references, extending the analytical value of existing single-cell and spatial gene-expression atlases.

works.title: Structured multi-view relational learning for drug response prediction
works.abstract: Drug response prediction (DRP) requires models that jointly characterize molecular drug structure and heterogeneous cellular states. Although recent deep learning approaches have integrated multi-omics profiles with drug representations, many treat omics views as parallel feature sources or merge them before relational modeling, which can weaken omics-view-specific cell-line relation structures. Here, we propose MulDR, a structured multi-view relational learning framework that preserves omics-view-specific cell-line relation structures before drug-conditioned cell-drug interaction. MulDR constructs separate relation structures for pathway activity, gene expression, mutation, and DNA methylation, learns view-specific relational cell representations, and uses complementary motif-level, geometry-aware molecular graph, and Morgan fingerprint drug representations to condition their fusion. With this design, cell-line similarity remains view-dependent until the interaction stage, rather than being prematurely compressed into a single feature or relation space. Extensive experiments show that MulDR consistently outperforms representative and recent baselines under the same evaluation protocol, reducing root mean square error by 6.07% relative to the strongest baseline. Cold-start evaluations on unseen drugs and cell lines further show that MulDR generalizes to previously unseen entities, while ablation studies show that removing either view-specific relational modeling or drug-conditioned fusion consistently compromises predictive performance. Together, these results suggest that preserving omics-specific cell-line relations before drug-conditioned interaction modeling provides an effective strategy for robust DRP.

works.title: scYOU: a multi-scale yoked optimization and unsupervised framework for analysis of cellular heterogeneity and complex-associated protein module recovery
works.abstract: Advances in high-resolution proteomic technologies are enabling systematic characterization of cellular heterogeneity and protein functional programs at increasing depth. However, existing computational approaches typically focus on either cell-level organization or protein-level structure, lacking a unified framework that jointly models both entities. Here we present scYOU, a multi-scale yoked optimization and unsupervised framework that simultaneously captures cellular heterogeneity and protein functional organization through a dual-channel neural network architecture. scYOU learns cell and protein embeddings in parallel while coupling the two views through a supercell-constrained alignment strategy. Supercells are constructed based on high-order expression similarity and define grouping structures over cells. A dual-channel alignment objective is imposed at the reconstruction level, such that reconstructed expression profiles of cells within the same supercell are encouraged to converge, whereas those from different supercells remain separable. On the protein side, Gene Ontology-derived functional similarity priors regularize protein embeddings to preserve molecular biological consistency. Across diverse benchmark datasets, scYOU achieves strong and relatively consistent clustering performance together with improved embedding separability, while the learned protein representations support embedding-guided refinement of existing interaction networks and the recovery of complex-associated protein modules. These results establish scYOU as a structurally coupled, multi-level representation learning framework for proteomic data, and highlight the importance of jointly modeling cellular heterogeneity and protein functional modules within a unified computational paradigm. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/anchor-hue/scYou.

works.title: RFhap: accurate alignment-free long-read phasing for improved diploid de novo assembly
works.abstract: Haplotype-resolved de novo assemblies enable genome-wide separation of maternal and paternal variation, improving the interpretation of complex variants relevant to human disease. Trio-aware assemblers such as Hifiasm-Trio leverage parental short reads by deriving parent-specific k-mers to guide phasing within the long-read assembly graph; however, fixed k-mer length and heuristics cannot be optimal in the presence of sequencing errors and graph complexity in repetitive regions, contributing to phasing errors and reduced haplotype-resolved contiguity. Here we present RFhap, a trio-based long-read phasing method that integrates multi-k-mer parent-specific markers with an alignment-free k-mer lookup engine and a random forest classifier to assign long reads to maternal, paternal, or unknown haplotypes prior to de novo assembly. We benchmarked RFhap on four human trio datasets from the Human Pangenome project spanning two ONT chemistries (R10.4 and R9.4.1). Using Merqury to evaluate downstream assemblies, RFhap nearly doubled corrected haplotype NG50 (mean 24.3 Mb vs. 13.1 Mb) and halved switch error rates (mean 0.111% vs. 0.236%) relative to Hifiasm-Trio, while remaining competitive in consensus QV and parental k-mer completeness. Consistent with improved phasing, RFhap reduced long-switch errors by ~ 3-fold across datasets, particularly within interspersed repeats. RFhap improves phasing accuracy from standard trio data, representing a step toward accurate and automated diploid human de novo assembly from long reads.

works.title: Routine susceptibility panels predict reserve-antibiotic resistance across ESKAPE pathogens: an ontology-anchored machine learning analysis with cross-species transfer
works.abstract: Abstract Resistance to reserve antibiotics such as carbapenems, glycopeptides, and oxazolidinones is the most consequential and least measured part of antimicrobial resistance. We asked whether resistance to these last-line agents can be predicted from the routine susceptibility panel that laboratories already produce, whether the predictive signal reflects shared resistance mechanisms, and whether it generalises across species. Using per-isolate susceptibility data for seven high-priority bacterial pathogens from a public bacterial bioinformatics resource (about 24,000 isolates), we built gradient-boosted models that predict resistance to each antibiotic from the rest of the panel, with every agent annotated for drug class and mechanism from a curated resistance ontology. Of 220 candidate pathogen-antibiotic pairs, 73 met a pre-specified eligibility rule and were evaluated by five-fold cross-validation. Resistance was broadly predictable (mean area under the curve 0.80 across the 73 models; 0.82 for reserve agents), reaching 0.90 for carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae and 0.97 for glycopeptide and oxazolidinone resistance in Enterococcus faecium. Performance was largely retained after same-class predictors were removed, indicating genuine cross-class co-resistance, and carbapenem resistance transferred across Gram-negative species. Routine panels therefore carry a strong, mechanism-aware signal for reserve-drug resistance.

works.title: Spatial transcriptomics landscape of livers from patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
works.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) progression involves heterogeneous responses and coordinated interactions among parenchymal and nonparenchymal cells. Single-cell transcriptomics has advanced our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, while spatial omics maps molecular signatures within tissue architecture, enabling inference of cell–cell and ligand–receptor interactions, particularly those involving macrophages in MASH. Here, we aimed to characterize spatially resolved transcriptomic alterations in hepatocyte-, hepatic stellate cell (HSC)-, and immune cell-enriched regions in individuals with obesity. We further sought to validate these signatures using public single-cell level RNA sequencing datasets and protein analyses and assess their clinical associations and changes following bariatric surgery. We performed spatial transcriptomic profiling of human liver tissues using the GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler in 16 patients with MASH across fibrosis stages and eight NonMASH controls. Regions of interest (ROIs) enriched for hepatocytes, immune cells, and HSCs were defined by immunofluorescence-guided pathological annotation. In addition to various bioinformatic analyses on spatial transcriptomic data, we integrated our data with several other public datasets. Finally, the study findings were further validated at the protein level. Each hepatic ROI exhibited distinct molecular alterations during MASH progression. Cytochrome P450 genes were significantly downregulated in hepatocyte-, HSC- and immune cell-enriched ROIs, and negatively correlated with the expression of nuclear receptor and pro-inflammatory genes. With advanced fibrosis in MASH, nonparenchymal ROIs showed marked mitochondrial dysfunction. Ligand‒receptor analysis revealed disrupted inter-regional communication (e.g. loss of protective signals and enhanced pro-fibrotic interactions). Notably, IL32 was consistently upregulated across all three ROI types in MASH versus NonMASH. In addition to validation using public single-cell level datasets, we identified 19 MASH-associated genes, whose expression was correlated with clinical and histologic parameters and reversed following bariatric surgery. Among the key genes identified in our analysis, we selectively validated the hepatic expression of CYP1A2, IL32, and S100A8/9 at the protein level in patients with MASH. Our results reveal compartment-specific metabolic and inflammatory reprogramming in human MASH, highlighting CYP450 suppression, immune activation, disrupted intercellular signaling, and reversibility after bariatric surgery, thereby providing therapeutic implications.

works.title: Clinico-genomic determinants of relapse in metachronous colorectal cancer metastases
works.abstract: Abstract Background Given the growing use of cancer screening, colorectal tumors are increasingly diagnosed before metastasizing to distant organs. However, up to 25% of patients with early-stage colorectal cancer later develop metachronous metastases – often years after primary tumor resection. When limited to the liver, they remain potentially curable by surgery, but outcomes following curative-intent resection vary substantially: some patients remain durably disease-free, whereas others relapse within months. Clinico-genomic determinants of this heterogeneity are not well understood, and genomic markers to personalize surgical decisions in patients with metachronous liver metastases are lacking. Methods We assembled a deeply annotated cohort of 41 colorectal cancer patients undergoing resection of metachronous liver metastases – with whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing of metastases and matched primary tumors (where available) and structured annotations of their longitudinal clinical trajectories, including a median follow-up of 66.4 months, relapse after metastatic surgery, adjuvant therapies, radiologic assessments, and blood-based markers. We further dissected relapse-associated genomic features in five independent datasets. Results Early relapse (< 12 months) correlated with a larger number of metachronous liver metastases and a characteristic copy-number pattern involving loss of arms 3p and 5q. Metastases with late/no relapse were characterized by multi-hit APC mutations. These genomic features also correlated with significant differences in relapse-free survival after metastatic surgery, and they were consistent between patients with and without adjuvant therapy for their primary and metastatic tumors. Early-relapsing metastases typically harbored an accumulation of multiple relapse-associated genomic changes. Moreover, metachronous metastases differed in genomic characteristics from synchronous metastases in an independent cohort, exhibiting a higher frequency of 5q loss and a higher burden of copy-number alterations relative to their matched primaries, suggesting continued evolution after primary-tumor resection. Transcriptomically, relapse-associated copy-number changes correlated with gene-dosage effects on the respective arms and differential expression of genes related to proliferation and metabolism. They also correlated with advanced disease and shorter survival in two independent datasets. Conclusions Our study characterizes the clinico-genomic basis of early relapse in metachronous liver metastases. Ultimately, these features could help identify patients with a high propensity to relapse after surgery and personalize the management of colorectal cancer patients with metachronous liver metastases.

works.title: Accelerated and comprehensive pediatric cancer profiling using whole-genome sequencing with adaptive sampling
works.abstract: Abstract Background Timely and comprehensive molecular classification is essential for therapeutic decision-making in pediatric oncology, yet current diagnostic workflows rely on multi-step, time- and resource-intensive testing strategies. We present a standardized whole-genome sequencing approach with adaptive sampling (AS-WGS) using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) optimized for pediatric cancers, that enables rapid and comprehensive molecular profiling in a single assay. Methods We designed an AS-WGS panel comprising 380 clinically relevant loci that we applied to the sequencing of 36 pediatric cancer and control samples. To support real-time interpretation, we developed an open-source bioinformatic pipeline (nf-core-oncoseq) enabling on-the-fly analysis during sequencing. We compared the AS-WGS results to those obtained by standard clinical assays, including exome and transcriptome sequencing. Results AS-WGS achieved somatic-grade coverage (mean 172X) in target regions while maintaining pan-genomic coverage (18X), thus supporting genome-wide copy number and methylation analyses. AS-WGS reliably detected all classes of clinically actionable alterations including fusion genes (20/20), small variants (SNVs and indels, in 58/59 mutated genes) and large CNVs (20/21). SNVs were robustly captured down to a 5% allelic frequency, similar to clinical exome sequencing. The PCR-free workflow supported methylation-based tumor classification, providing orthogonal confirmation of hematological and solid tumor subtypes in 9/11 acute lymphoblastic leukemias and in 8/12 solid tumors. All clonal alterations were identified with >5 supporting reads from data generated in the first 24 hours of sequencing (20/20 fusions and 47/47 SNVs with allelic frequencies > 25%), with some, such as large CNVs and methylation predictions, detected within the first hour. Conclusions Our results show that applying AS-WGS to pediatric hematological and solid tumors supports the rapid identification of all classes of genomic alterations and enables methylation-based classification in a single assay. Future efforts aimed at clinical translation will establish its position within the current multi-assay diagnostic landscape.

works.title: Individuals with autism-associated intellectual disability have an increased burden of de novo variants in cis-regulatory elements of glutamatergic neurons
works.abstract: Despite the trait of autism being strongly heritable, with many genes now implicated in its causation, the ability to make a clinical diagnosis in an affected individual remains limited. In this study, we sought to understand how DNA sequence variation in the non-coding majority of the human genome contributes to autism-associated intellectual disability (ID), We studied whole genome sequencing data from 20,366 individuals, in whom 709,222 de novo variants (DNVs) were identified. We tested the genomic distributions and properties of the DNVs in individuals with autism and ID compared with neurotypical study participants. We found enrichment of DNVs at cis -regulatory elements (CREs) across all somatic cell types in both the neurodivergent and neurotypical groups, attributable to the deamination of 5-methylcytosine at CG dinucleotide-dense CREs. In neurodivergent individuals with or without ID, the DNVs were enriched at genes implicated in autism/ID at promoter-proximal CREs of brain cell types specifically. Since the properties of these DNVs were not distinct enough to explain why some individuals had autism or ID, we performed a multivariate category-wide association study (CWAS), which revealed enrichment of DNVs in CREs of glutamatergic neurons in individuals with ID. A Random Forest analysis uncovered an increased burden of these events in individuals within the ID subgroup. Our findings support a model in which non-coding variants contribute to the oligogenic heritability of ID, through influences on the transcriptional regulation of glutamatergic neurons.

works.title: Diet-induced programmable GLP-1 delivery by synthetic bacteria enhances anti-obesity efficacy with reduced gut bacterial taxa harboring GLP-1 inactivation potential
works.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin hormone that controls energy homeostasis, and impaired GLP-1 secretion or responsiveness is associated with metabolic diseases. Much effort has been made to develop long-lasting GLP-1-based therapeutics, whereas frequently associated with drug resistance and side effects. GLP-1 is predominantly released postprandially by enteroendocrine cells, while programmable GLP-1 delivery is rarely explored. Herein, genetically engineered probiotic bacteria for diet-induced programmable GLP-1 delivery were developed. The therapeutic efficacy of diet-induced and constitutive GLP-1 delivery was compared in a murine model of obesity, followed by microbiome profiling and functional characterization of gut bacterial GLP-1-degrading enzymes. In murine model of obesity, the anti-adiposity and anti-steatosis effects of diet-induced programmable GLP-1 delivery by synthetic bacteria were greater than that of microbial persistent GLP-1 delivery. Notably, genes encoding microbe-derived GLP-1 peptidase isoenzymes were discovered in gut bacteria specifically enriched by persistent GLP-1 delivery in murine and clinical studies, while diet-induced GLP-1 delivery minimized the abundance of these gut bacteria with GLP-1 inactivation potential. Our findings provide insights into host-microbiome-therapeutic interactions, and highlight programmable delivery strategies for peptide-based therapeutics.

works.title: RNASTOP: A Deep Learning Framework for mRNA Chemical Stability Prediction and Optimization
works.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines offer promising therapeutic potential for combating various diseases, yet their inherent chemical instability hampers long-term efficacy. Although several methods have been developed to predict mRNA degradation, they often suffer from limited accuracy and lack the capability for rational codon optimization. Here, we propose RNASTOP, a novel framework that integrates deep learning with heuristic search to simultaneously predict and optimize mRNA chemical stability. RNASTOP achieves a 13% improvement in accuracy over the top-performing model on the Stanford OpenVaccine competition dataset and demonstrates robust generalization in predicting full-length mRNA degradation. When applied to mRNA codon optimization, RNASTOP reduces the minimum free energy of the varicella-zoster virus vaccine sequence by 75.73% while maintaining high translation efficiency. Overall, RNASTOP serves as a powerful tool for predicting and optimizing mRNA chemical stability, accelerating the development of mRNA therapeutics. The source code of RNASTOP is available at https://github.com/xlab-BioAI/RNASTOP.

works.title: AbLWR: a context-aware listwise ranking framework for antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction via positive-unlabeled learning
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity is fundamental to therapeutic design and the rapid response to evolving pathogens. However, current computational approaches predominantly formulate this as a point-wise regression task. This paradigm struggles to discriminate subtle affinity differences among highly homologous variants and lacks the global context necessary to effectively prioritize top-tier candidates. Furthermore, the field is severely constrained by label sparsity. Although sequence data is abundant, experimentally verified affinities are scarce, leaving a massive pool of unverified antibody-antigen structural interactions unexploited by standard supervised paradigms. RESULTS: We propose AbLWR (Antibody-antigen binding affinity Listwise Ranking), a novel framework that reformulates the conventional affinity regression task as a listwise ranking problem to directly optimize candidate prioritization. To mitigate label sparsity, AbLWR incorporates a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning mechanism, leveraging a dual-level contrastive objective and meta-optimized label refinement to distill robust structural representations from vast unlabeled data. To accommodate antigenic variation, we employ a homologous antigen sampling strategy coupled with a Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) module, which explicitly models inter-sample dependencies within training lists to capture subtle affinity nuances. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that AbLWR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art sequence-, structure-, and complex-based baselines. It improves the Full Rank Accuracy (FRA) by approximately 8% compared to the strongest baseline in randomized cross-validation, and exhibits strong robustness in out-of-distribution scenarios involving distinct antigen and antibody clusters. Case studies on Influenza Viruses and Human Interleukin-33 further validate its practical utility. Specifically, AbLWR successfully tracks affinity drops caused by antigenic drift and immediately captures optimal binders in simulated wet-lab screening. AVAILABILITY: Source code and datasets are freely available at https://github.com/Josie-xufan/AbLWR.

works.title: spaDWGCN: a spatial distance weighted graph convolution network for accurate spatial tissue structure identification
works.abstract: The continuous development of spatial transcriptomics enables us to obtain gene expression matrices alongside spatial coordinate labels for cells or spots, providing tools for understanding spatial tissue microenvironments and spatially resolved cell-cell interactions. Although numerous methods have been developed to identify spatial tissue architecture, most of them adopt binary adjacency matrices that treat all neighboring cells equally, and few comprehensively incorporate distance information into both graph construction and feature representation.
