Here we introduce spaDWGCN, a spatial distance weighted graph convolutional network algorithm that takes cellular gene expression and microenvironment composition as inputs. This approach introduces fine-grained distance weighting at two levels: replacing the conventional 0-1 binary adjacency matrix with a distance-weighted adjacency matrix at the graph level, and substituting the neighbor count matrix with a distance-weighted microenvironment composition matrix at the feature level. Furthermore, spaDWGCN jointly models gene expression and microenvironment composition through separate graph convolutional network branches and trainable fusion, integrating transcriptional patterns with their local neighborhood context within a unified framework. Experiments on spatial transcriptomics multi-platform datasets, including MERFISH, STARmap, Stereo-seq, Slide-seqV2, and 10× Visium, demonstrate that this distance-weighted strategy achieves competitive performance in spatial domain identification and other downstream analyses.

works.title: How far can you borrow? Divergence limits of cross-species Gene Ontology enrichment in non-model organisms
works.abstract: Functional interpretation of omics data from non-model species almost always relies on borrowing Gene Ontology (GO) annotations from a model organism-often a distant one (Arabidopsis for plants, zebrafish or human for fish)-and running enrichment analysis on inferred orthologs. How far this practice can be pushed before the enrichment result degrades has never been quantified at the level practitioners use. We present the first systematic benchmark of the divergence-tolerance of cross-species GO-transfer enrichment, across six focal species spanning three eukaryotic kingdoms, each with 15-22 reference species tiling a continuous phylogenetic gradient. Set-level fidelity-measured as redundancy-robust Wang semantic similarity between transferred and experimental-truth enriched term sets-declines monotonically with distance, collapsing to chance at the clade boundary in some panels (fish, rice) while remaining well above it in others (insect, fungi, mammal) (half-collapse identity, ID50, ~40%-59%). At fixed distance, a richer reference raises recall but lowers precision, quantifying a long-recognized but unresolved trade-off. Conserved processes transfer reliably to distant references whereas taxon-specific processes do not, a pattern consistent across all six focal species tested. Whole-genome duplication degrades transfer only when ohnolog retention is high, showing up as sensitivity to the orthology method rather than a steeper decline. An independent, GO-free measure of expression conservation supports the curves in vertebrates. We condense these results into a focal-species × distance reliability guide and a step-by-step decision protocol that let researchers judge, before analysis, whether borrowed-GO enrichment can be trusted for their species and question.

works.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics
works.abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

works.title: A new noninvasive prenatal paternity test based on double nucleotide polymorphisms abates sequencing uncertainties and improves sensitivity
works.abstract: Noninvasive prenatal paternity testing (NIPAT) based on fetal cell-free DNA (fetal cfDNA) has gained increasing relevance in forensic genetics. However, its applicability and reliability are often limited by the low fetal DNA fraction and by high-throughput sequencing errors that can be misinterpreted as inherited paternal variants. Here, we present NEWPAT, a novel NIPAT approach based on Double Nucleotide Polymorphisms (DNPs), i.e. biallelic variants composed of two adjacent nucleotides arising from a single mutational event. These markers offer a key advantage compared to single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs): the likelihood of both positions being affected by independent sequencing errors is extremely low, thus improving the specificity of fetal DNA detection. We develop a targeted amplicon-based panel including 979 markers (845 autosomal and 80 X Chromosome DNPs, plus 54 Y SNPs), and test at depths ranging from 1,000× to 10,000× on 42 individuals, including genomic DNA from 4 families, 2 artificial maternal-child mixtures simulating cfDNA and actual cfDNA from 12 pregnant women plus the putative biological fathers. We observe a DNP sequencing error rate of 8.9×10 -5 , i.e. ~12 times lower than the observed single base error rate. By exploiting the full range of sequencing depths at loci supporting the fetal genotype, we obtain Combined Paternity Index curves that consistently lead to the correct paternity attribution or exclusion in all true or false mother-father pairs. Notably, NEWPAT proves effective even at fetal cfDNA levels as low as 0.2%, when existing SNP-based protocols lead to inconclusive results, offering a highly sensitive and accurate NIPAT strategy.

works.title: Developmental transcriptomic analysis of primary mouse cortical neurons reveals sex-specific expression of neuropeptides
works.abstract: Primary neuronal cultures derived from mouse tissue serve as an essential model for investigating neuronal development and function. Despite this, comprehensive developmental and sex-specific transcriptomic profiles in primary neurons have not been defined. Here, we perform multiplexed RNA sequencing of neurons derived from male and female cortices across time. We validate this approach by assessing established neuronal maturation genes and identify highly stable genes to serve as controls across development. Next, using linear modeling and temporal regression, we define developmentally regulated transcripts, longitudinal expression dynamics, and gene signatures associated with transition states throughout development. Unexpectedly, this also reveals sex-specific effects on autosomal genes that emerge only after neuronal maturation even in the absence of in vivo cues. Most notably, neuropeptide genes Cortistatin and Neurokinin A are more highly expressed in female neurons. Furthermore, exposure to these neuropeptides elicits distinct transcriptional responses in male- versus female-derived cultures. These findings provide a valuable resource and reveal sex-specific autosomal transcriptional signatures that emerge in neurons maintained ex vivo.

works.title: CORE clonotypes: a reproducible structural component of the peripheral TCR repertoire revealed through variation in blood processing times
works.abstract: High-throughput T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing is widely used for immune profiling, yet repertoire measurements remain sensitive to pre-analytical variables that can affect reproducibility and downstream interpretation. Among these variables, delays between blood collection and sample processing may alter detectable repertoire composition, particularly among low-frequency clonotypes. Here, we use processing-delay variability as a structured technical perturbation to examine organizational features of the peripheral TCR repertoire. We analyzed peripheral blood TCRβ repertoires from 211 patients with newly diagnosed colorectal cancer, comparing samples processed shortly after blood collection with samples subjected to extended processing delays. Delayed processing was associated with reduced clonotype richness, depletion of singleton clonotypes, and altered diversity distributions, indicating preferential loss of low-frequency repertoire elements under prolonged handling conditions. Within this framework, we defined CORE clonotypes (COnsistent Repertoire Elements) operationally as amino-acid-identical CDR3β sequences detected in both processing groups. We characterized CORE clonotypes across multiple analytical levels, including abundance distributions, V/J gene usage, amino-acid composition, nucleotide redundancy, codon usage, biochemical properties, and correlation-network structure. CORE clonotypes were largely distinct from abundance-matched clonotype sets, indicating that reproducible detection across perturbation conditions is not explained solely by clonotype abundance. At the nucleotide level, CORE clonotypes exhibited elevated synonymous sequence diversity while maintaining conserved amino-acid composition across processing conditions. Following sequencing-depth normalization, CORE clonotypes showed reduced codon-usage divergence and narrower distributions across multiple biochemical properties relative to group-unique clonotypes. Correlation-network analysis further identified a small CORE-associated subnetwork enriched for previously annotated antigen associations compared with randomized controls. These findings suggest that technical perturbations can reveal reproducibly detected, non-random repertoire elements with distinct organizational properties across multiple molecular levels. More broadly, this work highlights the value of pre-analytical variability as a tool for characterizing reproducible repertoire structure in immune repertoire sequencing studies.

works.title: Extracting candidate motif patterns for multiple RNA modifications using direct RNA sequencing
works.abstract: RNA modifications have emerged as key regulators of virtually all aspects of RNA biology, driving growing interest in computational approaches for their transcriptome-wide detection. For some RNA modifications, the search space can be reduced by exploiting characteristic sequence motifs, as exemplified by the canonical DRACH motif associated with m⁶A. However, comparable sequence preferences remain largely unknown for most other RNA modifications, making systematic motif discovery considerably more challenging. Here, we applied exponential population analysis to direct RNA sequencing data from HEK293T cells and peripheral human blood to identify candidate motif patterns for pseudouridine (Ψ), inosine (I), and 5-methylcytosine (m⁵C). Our results demonstrate that exponential population analysis provides a systematic framework for identifying candidate motif patterns from nanopore-derived RNA modification predictions, thereby prioritizing sequence contexts for future biological validation.

works.title: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease: The complete molecular architecture for the PKHD1 gene and its protein
works.abstract: Fibrocystin/polyductin is a large single-pass transmembrane glycoprotein involved in tubulogenesis and maintenance of the epithelium, where disease-causing variants in its encoding gene PKHD1 cause autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD).While enormous experimental efforts have been taken to characterize proteins involved in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, the structural and molecular basis of fibrocystin has lagged behind with no known mechanistic models.Here, our study introduces the first idealized molecular model of fibrocystin, where we confirm the established domain architecture and refine the nomenclature of unresolved regions.Using our molecular model, we show that disease-causing missense variants tend to be buried and impose significant loss-of-function effects to the monomer.Furthermore, our molecular model suggests that the protective kidney survival outcomes associated with missense variants from amino acids 709-1837 are likely a result of their surface exposure on the IPT domains.Likewise, the protective hepatic outcomes of missense variants occurring in amino acids 1838-2624 are predicted to impose weakly destabilizing effects compared to all other functional classes of variants.Overall, our idealized model is the first to provide potential hypotheses addressing the broad diversity of phenotypes, thereby laying a foundation for basic and translational efforts for ARPKD.

works.title: Temporal analysis of clinical variant reclassification (2012–2025)
works.abstract: ClinVar is the primary archive for human genetic variant classifications, yet existing studies lack a longitudinal perspective of its evolution, often conflating clinical reinterpretation of variant pathogenicity with variant reclassification resulting from database schema evolution. We systematically characterized ClinVar’s 13-year history (2012–2025), analyzing 3.68 million variants across 148 monthly snapshots using both Reference ClinVar (RCV)- and Variation ClinVar (VCV)-formatted Extensible Markup Language (XML) files. An era-stratified heuristic framework was developed to distinguish schema-driven reclassification artifacts from evidence-based clinical reinterpretation. We additionally assessed inter-submitter concordance, disease-domain reclassification patterns, and American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) evidence documentation. Overall, 9.3% of variants underwent at least one change in aggregate classification category; however, only 0.68% (25,105 variants) ever underwent a medically significant change — that is, a change crossing the clinical actionability boundary between pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) and variant of uncertain significance/benign/likely benign (VUS/B/LB), including 6,340 variants that underwent a drastic pathogenic-to-benign (or vice versa) switch. Accounting for censoring, the cumulative incidence of first reclassification was 2.5% at one year and 15.5% at five years after a variant’s first appearance. We identified three distinct schema eras involving over 120 structural database changes that impact data interpretation, with 2.6% of all reclassification events attributable to the RCV-to-VCV format transition. Reclassification rates were significantly higher in cancer-related genes than in other genes (16.6% vs. 8.2%) and in higher- than in lower-prevalence Mendelian disease variants (19.7% vs. 9.2%). Among multi-submitter variants, 72.1% were concordant while 17.6% maintained conflicting interpretations. Of 697,698 reclassification events, 33.2% resulted from submitter reinterpretation and 18.3% from new-submitter-driven category shifts. Population-frequency releases (the Exome Aggregation Consortium [ExAC] and the Genome Aggregation Database [gnomAD]) and functional evidence from high-throughput saturation mutagenesis and targeted biochemical assays were identified as important contributors to reclassification. Our findings support the need for domain-specific variant reassessment intervals and reinforce the importance of diverse population reference datasets and high-throughput functional assays to minimize classification uncertainty. We also published an open-source pipeline and visualization framework to enable reproducible, era-aware temporal analysis of clinical variant reclassification.

works.title: Dietary restriction remodels the melanoma immune microenvironment and enhances immunotherapy response with spatial association of SELE+ HEVs and NKT-like cells
works.abstract: Dietary restriction (DR) can influence cancer progression by remodeling the tumor microenvironment (TME), but its immunomodulatory effects and underlying mechanisms in melanoma remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize DR-associated transcriptional and cellular changes in melanoma and determine their relevance to prognosis and immunotherapy response. We integrated bulk transcriptomic, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomic, and experimental data to establish and validate a transcriptome-derived dietary restriction score (DRS) that quantifies DR-associated transcriptional programs. The association of DRS with clinical outcomes and immunotherapy response was evaluated across multiple cohorts. Mouse melanoma models were used to assess the effects of DR on tumor growth and anti-PD-1 efficacy. Cellular enrichment, functional states, spatial colocalization, and intercellular communication were analyzed to identify DR-responsive cell populations and their potential interactions within the melanoma TME. A high DRS was associated with favorable prognosis and improved response to immunotherapy in human melanoma. In mouse models, DR suppressed melanoma growth through immune-dependent mechanisms and enhanced the therapeutic efficacy of anti-PD-1 treatment. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identified cytotoxic natural killer T (NKT)-like cells and SELE⁺ high endothelial venule (HEV) cells as DR-responsive populations enriched in DRS-high tumors. These populations were associated with enhanced anti-tumor immunity and favorable immunotherapy outcomes. Spatial analysis further revealed significant colocalization between NKT-like cells and SELE⁺ HEV cells in DRS-high tumors, whereas this pattern was not observed in DRS-low tumors. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested that SELE⁺ HEV cells may promote NKT-like cell recruitment and activation through ICAM1-ITGAL/ITGB2 signaling. These findings identify a DR-associated immunovascular axis involving SELE⁺ HEV cells and cytotoxic NKT-like cells that may enhance lymphocyte recruitment, activation, and responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. The DRS provides a transcriptomic framework for characterizing DR-associated TME remodeling and supports further investigation of dietary restriction as a potential adjunctive strategy for melanoma immunotherapy.

works.title: BioHarness: substrate-aware evidence assembly for biomedical question answering across literature, knowledge bases, and biological atlases
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: Biomedical question answering often requires evidence beyond topically retrieved literature, including gene alias resolution, database identifier normalization, and atlas-derived biological measurements. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems typically follow a fixed workflow and lack an explicit mechanism for deciding when retrieved text is sufficient, when biomedical entity mapping is needed, or when executable evidence assembly over structured measurements should be invoked. This motivates a substrate-aware large language model (LLM) harness that selectively assembles sufficient evidence by combining literature retrieval, biomedical entity mapping, and access to atlas-derived measurements. RESULTS: We introduce BioHarness, an LLM harness for staged biomedical evidence assembly across literature retrieval, biomedical entity-mapping resources, and atlas-derived structured measurements. Across 22 123 biomedical QA items spanning seven answer formats, BioHarness improves the pooled score from 62.2 to 67.2 over the strongest baseline. Ablations, case studies, and backbone-scaling analyses show that these gains arise from repairing evidence-substrate mismatches through reranking, entity grounding, and structured measurement access, rather than from indiscriminately invoking more reasoning steps, retrieving additional literature, or relying on a particular answer-model scale. Comparisons with the frontier models and harness show that BioHarness, despite using an open-weight backbone with only 3B active parameters, approaches frontier-level performance on selected literature QA tasks and outperforms frontier harnesses without web access on biomedical identifier and locus lookup. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code, reproducible benchmarking scripts, and processed benchmark data required to reproduce all results in this study are publicly available under an open-source license, together with the exat configuration, model versions, and decoding settings used in our experiments. In addition, we developed a prototype web demo (https://xcompass.scimatrix.cn/) that illustrates how BioHarness can be used in an interactive biomedical QA setting.

works.title: LRP2: a proteogenomics pipeline for long-read informed protein isoform analysis and discovery
works.abstract: SUMMARY: Most human genes produce multiple RNA isoforms, yet it remains unclear which isoforms are translated into stable, functional proteins. Long-read RNA sequencing resolves full-length transcript structures and, when paired with mass spectrometry, can provide empirical evidence of isoform translation. Despite this opportunity, comprehensive workflows integrating isoform discovery, open reading frame prediction, peptide identification, and protein inference remain limited, leaving users to handle these steps piecemeal. Here, we present LRP2, a modular, end-to-end long-read proteogenomics pipeline built in Nextflow. LRP2 scales transcript discovery to hundreds of samples via PacBio's latest Isocall tool, removes technical artifacts with SQANTI QC, generates and classifies predicted proteomes via CPAT and SQANTI Protein, performs multi-group differential expression and usage analysis via edgeR, DRIMSeq, and a long-read adaptation of LeafCutter, and integrates protein-level evidence from DDA and DIA MS data through FragPipe. For cross-dataset comparison of novel isoforms, LRP2 employs deterministic splice junction, coordinate-based isoform identifiers. Used as an integrated pipeline, LRP2 enables the detection of novel peptides and improves protein isoform inference to confirm protein isoform translation. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: LRP2 is freely available as a modular Nextflow pipeline at https://github.com/sheynkman-lab/LRP2 (v2.0.0, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22795865). LRP2 supports Docker, Apptainer/Singularity, and Conda environments with GENCODE references.

works.title: From SELEX to sequencing: uncovering enriched aptamers with next-generation sequencing and bioinformatics
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: The combinatorial chemistry process called systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) enables the selection of aptamers against different targets. The integration of next-generation sequencing (NGS) into SELEX workflows represents a powerful strategy to enhance the identification and prioritization of target-binding aptamers. In this study, we present an optimized computational approach for the NGS-based analysis of enriched aptamer pools generated through SELEX. It encompasses sequencing library preparation, sequence data preprocessing, clustering, multiple sequence alignment, phylogenetic analysis, and secondary structure prediction. RESULTS: To identify target-specific aptamers, two comparative analysis strategies were implemented. In the first strategy, sequences detected in the negative selection pool were removed from the positive selection pool to eliminate nonspecific binders, resulting in six distinct sequence clusters. In the second approach, all sequences were retained, and cluster distributions were compared between the positive and negative selection pools, identifying seven clusters in the positive and six in the negative pool. Phylogenetic relationships and structural predictions enabled the selection of promising candidates, which were prioritized based on secondary structure, sequence abundance, and genetic distance from nonspecific binders. Binding specificity was assessed through dot blot assays, confirming that the selected aptamers exhibited strong specific binding to the target protein. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the NGS-guided workflow for aptamer discovery and highlight its value in streamlining candidate selection for downstream functional validation. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The data underlying this article will be shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author.

works.title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition
Tracing causal cascades underlying biological state changes
OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
works.abstract: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

works.title: Alignment of RNA secondary structures with arbitrary pseudoknots using structural sequences
works.abstract: Abstract Background Comparison of RNA secondary structures is fundamental for RNA classification, motif analysis, and evolutionary studies. While efficient methods exist for pseudoknot-free structures, the comparison of RNA secondary structures with arbitrary pseudoknots remains computationally challenging. The aim of this study is to introduce a novel sequence-based representation and an associated alignment distance for efficiently comparing RNA secondary structures with arbitrary pseudoknots. Results We introduce a novel representation of RNA secondary structures with arbitrary pseudoknots based on integer sequences, called structural sequences. On this representation, we define the SERNA distance, an extension of the classical edit distance with structural correctness constraints, and prove that it is a metric. We present SERNAlign, an open-source tool that computes the SERNA distance using dynamic programming with quadratic time complexity. To evaluate the proposed distance, we conduct two complementary experiments within a clustering-based evaluation framework: classification of experimentally validated pseudoknot motifs, which directly targets the design goal of SERNA, and phylogenetic clustering of ribosomal RNAs as a robustness check against existing structural distances. Across both tasks, SERNA demonstrates competitive clustering performance with respect to state-of-the-art comparison methods, while providing improved discrimination in complex motif settings and significantly lower computational cost compared to structure-based approaches.

works.title: A kinematic interpretation of spatial expression gradients from single-snapshot spatial transcriptomics
works.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene expression across tissue position, but temporal or mechanistic interpretation of a spatial gradient requires an explicit model. We derive a kinematic interpretation for tissues with a stationary position-conditioned expression field and positive mean cell displacement along an anatomical axis. Under these assumptions, a gene’s gradient sign equals its net-production sign. The measured statistic remains a spatial gradient, and without an independent velocity estimate the framework does not recover absolute rates. We evaluate the framework on a human liver atlas with 16 standard-Visium sections, three matched Visium HD sections and companion single-nucleus RNA-seq; the primary cross-donor analysis uses eight live-donor sections. Gradient direction is reproducible: mean cross-donor correlation is 0.87 on a strict 66-gene panel and 0.67 on a broad 15,192-gene panel. On prespecified top-quartile subsets, cross-platform sign agreement is 14/14 genes for M2 and 13/14 for M6 ( n = 14 per donor); cross-pipeline agreement is 76%. Four diagnostics and a geometric argument show that the gene-gene coupling matrix is not stably identifiable or interpretable as a regulatory Jacobian from one sampled trajectory. In graded steatosis across four donors, GLUL , LYZ and ORM1 show consistent spatial-gradient responses to lipid, but wild-cluster calibration finds cluster-robust significance anticonservative; we report directional observations, not significant discoveries. On the mouse crypt-villus axis, all 15 canonical markers recover their expected directions on an anatomy-derived coordinate. The framework provides a reproducible, splicing-free estimator of spatial expression gradients applicable to imaging-based platforms. Under explicit steady-state and positive-flow assumptions, gradient direction has a kinematic interpretation as net-production direction; cross-sectional data establish gradient reproducibility, not time-resolved dynamics. Separating the observable from its conditional interpretation, and diagnosing the coupling matrix’s identification failure, defines both the method and its inferential boundary.

works.title: scDIG: an R Shiny application for interactive density-based gating of single-cell proteomic and transcriptomic data
works.abstract: Delineating biologically meaningful cell populations within single-cell embedding spaces requires methods that balance expert guidance with reproducibility. Current approaches range from subjective manual selection to fully automated algorithms that may obscure rare but biologically significant populations. We present scDIG, a Shiny-based tool that integrates bimodal index-driven feature selection, feature-weighted kernel density estimation, and interactive contour-based gating to define cell populations directly within two-dimensional projections of scRNA-seq and CITE-seq data. Applied to CITE-seq PBMC data from subjects in the Cardiovascular Assessment Virginia (CAVA) cohort, scDIG resolved transcriptionally distinct CD4⁺ T cell subpopulations within continuous embeddings not readily captured by conventional clustering and identified GZMB -enriched cytotoxic lymphocyte subsets from RNA expression data. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that defined gates correspond to coherent cell populations in high-dimensional feature space. s cDIG provides a robust, reproducible framework for density-based gating of single-cell data, bridging the interpretability of manual expert gating with the rigor of algorithmic population definition. The app is freely available for non-commercial use at https://au-cbgm-shiny.augusta.edu/gating , with source code at https://gitlab.com/pbombina/scdig .

works.title: PELICAN: a new bacteriophage genome annotation tool
works.abstract: Bacteriophages, or simply phages, are viruses that infect bacteria. They can serve as antibacterial agents, particularly against important bacterial pathogens. Accurate gene identification in phage genomes is essential for research and therapeutic applications. Detecting genes linked to lytic or lysogenic lifestyles, toxins, or bacterial fitness helps guide phage selection. We present PELICAN, a command-line tool for bacteriophage genome annotation. The PELICAN pipeline has four stages: (i) integration of multi-tool predictions; (ii) probabilistic and machine learning-based evaluation of non-consensus genes; (iii) resolution of overlapping predictions; and (iv) codon bias check of overlapped positions to produce a final annotation. For validation, we used reference phage genome annotations validated by transcriptomics and compared the results to those of other phage genome annotation tools. PELICAN had the best recall, but a higher false positive rate than some of the other tools. We present evidence that most of these false positives may be in fact true positives. Our evidence is primarily based on protein folding scores of the putative proteins coded in the predicted coding regions. PELICAN is a novel tool for bacteriophage genome annotation that provides improved gene recall and competitive F1 values compared to an existing similar tool.

works.title: Precision survival estimation in acute myeloid leukemia using evolutionary learning-derived microRNA signature
works.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains associated with poor long-term survival despite advances in targeted therapies. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate hematopoietic differentiation, apoptosis, and therapeutic resistance and may provide complementary markers of disease outcome. We applied the AML Survival Estimator, which integrates evolutionary feature selection with support vector regression, to expression profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas acute myeloid leukemia cohort, comprising 354 miRNA features from 156 patients and identified a 28-miRNA candidate panel. Linked clinical records documented 96 deaths and 60 censored observations; Kaplan-Meier median overall survival was 19.23 months. The panel-based Cox model achieved Harrell concordance of 0.718, a 24-month time-dependent area under the curve of 0.852, and an integrated Brier score of 0.164 over 6 to 36 months. Concordance was 0.645 for an age/sex model and 0.730 for the combined model. Permutation tests, size-matched random-panel controls, early-outcome sensitivity analyses, and calibration assessment further characterized performance. Qualitative target and pathway annotations highlighted candidate links to leukemogenesis and apoptosis. These findings identify a compact miRNA panel for AML prognostic research and support independent evaluation alongside established clinical and molecular risk models.

works.title: Dynamic networks can promote pro-sociality
Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
Making the case for a non-primary article
Near-complete assembly of wild emmer wheat unveils centromere reorganization during polyploid evolution
High false sign rates in transcriptome-wide association studies
works.abstract: Abstract Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to identify genes involved in complex traits and to infer the direction of gene effects on traits. However, despite their popularity, it remains unclear how accurately TWAS recover the true direction of a gene’s effect on a trait. Here we estimate the false sign rate of TWAS for plasma proteins, leveraging the expectation that increased gene expression should generally increase protein expression. We then extend this framework to complex traits, where loss-of-function burden tests provide the expected direction of effect. In both analyses, we observe high discordance with expectations, with TWAS showing a false sign rate of 23% for plasma proteins and 33% for complex traits. We propose that much of the sign discordance arises when expression quantitative trait loci in non-trait-relevant tissues tag haplotypes associated with traits in genome-wide association studies via distinct, tightly linked regulatory variants, yielding spurious TWAS associations with the correct genes but with unreliable direction of effect. These findings show that TWAS-based direction-of-effect estimates should be interpreted with caution and raise concerns about the reliability of TWAS more broadly.

works.title: Co-regulation confounds direction of genetic effects in transcriptome-wide association studies
Multi-omics analysis of high-grade serous ovarian cancers reveals heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns based upon clinico-genomic status
works.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by remarkable intratumoral heterogeneity and variable tissue architectures, dictating differential therapeutic responses. Although BRCA1/2 mutations correlate with improved responses to DNA-damaging agents, how BRCA genotype shapes the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated whole exome sequencing, total RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to profile a cohort of BRCA-mutated (BRCA-MT) and non-BRCA-mutated (BRCA-WT) HGSOC tumors. While bulk transcriptomics highlighted global phenotypic shifts, suggesting a more pro-inflammatory milieu in BRCA-MT tumors, spatially resolved analysis revealed how these differences manifest within specific tissue architectures. Integrated clustering revealed recurrent spatial transcriptional states across genotypes. Specifically, we identified a transcriptionally distinct immune-enriched region (IC7) characterized by low tumor purity, interferon signaling, and antigen-presentation programs. Reference-based RCTD deconvolution provided orthogonal computational support that IC7 was enriched for T/NK and dendritic cells relative to non-IC7 regions. At the patient level, the functional state of IC7 was highly BRCA-dependent: BRCA-MT tumors exhibited stronger enrichment of interferon-α/γ responses and inflammatory signaling than BRCA-WT tumors. Exploratory CellChat analysis further suggested genotype-associated differences in predicted immune-related signaling. We also identify a conserved structural interface between CAF-like region (IC3) and macrophage-rich region (IC4), accompanied by a predicted CXCL12-CXCR4 chemokine recruitment axis. Taken together, these findings support a model in which BRCA mutation status is associated with functional differences within broadly conserved spatial regions, rather than extensive reorganization of the overall spatial architecture. This spatially resolved framework identifies BRCA-associated immune transcriptional patterns in HGSOC and provides a basis for future mechanistic validation.

works.title: XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models
works.abstract: SUMMARY: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data in PDX models. XenoMix leverages the high sequence homology between human and mouse genomes to detect and quantify unexpected signal contributions originating from mouse DNA. Using ground truth mixtures, XenoMix achieved Pearson's correlation coefficients higher than 0.99. When applied to PDX data, we identified varying levels of mouse contamination originating from biological and technological variability. XenoMix establishes a critical quality control step in DNA methylation analysis of PDX models, and we show that the estimated contamination can be incorporated as a confounding variable in downstream analyses. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: XenoMix is available as a standalone R package from https://git.dkfz.de/b370/scepigen/XenoMix and as a module in the RnBeads software package.

works.title: BioSIFTR: functional inference from shallow shotgun sequencing using biome-specific genome catalogues benchmarked in gut microbiomes
works.abstract: Abstract Shallow shotgun sequencing is an accurate microbiome profiling method, but its use for functions is limited. BioSIFTR extrapolates shallow shotgun read mapping to precalculated pangenome functions in 15 MGnify biome-specific catalogues, which span host-associated and environmental microbiomes. We benchmarked BioSIFTR on synthetic communities and on three gut microbiomes — red junglefowl, mouse, and human — using matched deep shotgun and 16S rRNA metabarcoding data, outperforming similar approaches. Further validation will require matched benchmark datasets and is a priority for future work. BioSIFTR is thus a practical method for functional inference from cost-effective shallow shotgun sequencing, currently validated in gut microbiomes.

works.title: The Vizitig pangenome and pantranscriptome explorer
works.abstract: Vizitig is the first platform for real-time exploration and querying of DNA and RNA sequence de Bruijn graphs across many samples, unifying visualization, metadata, and flexible search. It constructs compacted colored de Bruijn graphs from raw sequencing reads and reference sequences and then provides an interactive web interface for graph exploration. It integrates raw and reference-based data, handles complex variation, and provides a human-readable feature-based (also referred to as metadata) query language with scalable graph loading. Its domain-specific query language supports composable searches combining sequences of arbitrary size, genomic features such as gene or exon identifiers, and experimental factors such as sample identifiers or abundance thresholds. On-demand subgraph loading retrieves only regions of interest, enabling interactive exploration of large data sets in the graphical user interface without loading the entire graph into memory. We demonstrate Vizitig's capabilities through case studies in pantranscriptomics and pangenomics. In pantranscriptomics, we recover fusion transcript breakpoints on long and short reads. In pangenomics, we explore sequence variations across yeast, rice, nematode, and human pangenomes. Vizitig scales from small virus genomes to human-scale pangenomes (our largest experiment comprises up to 20 assembled human haplotypes, on a laptop). Vizitig enables fast, reproducible analysis in both pangenomics and pantranscriptomics while providing a deployable and user-friendly working environment.

works.title: Base composition reflects RNA polymerase II displacement
works.abstract: RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcribes all protein-coding and many non-protein-coding genes in the genome. Pol II transcription termination is crucial for RNA maturation and, when disrupted, can lead to altered RNA processing and RNA export. Termination involves two intertwined processes: RNA cleavage and Pol II release from the DNA (displacement). Despite its importance, the exact mechanisms underlying Pol II displacement from the DNA remain poorly understood. Moreover, under certain cellular stress conditions, there is a partial failure of cleavage, leading to a shift of the position of displacement further downstream, a phenomenon known as readthrough transcription. We present a systematic analysis of Pol II termination across cell types and species and provide novel insights into the mechanism of displacement. Using a probabilistic mixture model to quantify Pol II dynamics across entire gene bodies from nascent RNA sequencing data, we find that genes fall into two classes defined by conserved base composition patterns near the displacement site. Both classes share a T-rich region upstream of displacement, and one class additionally carries a GC-rich region surrounding displacement. We find that GC-rich predisplacement regions have more accessible chromatin and higher levels of phospho-threonine 4 on the CTD of Pol II. Additionally, we find that displacement at genes with only the upstream T-rich pattern are more likely to be affected by perturbations that alter displacement, including heat shock, viral infection, kinase inhibition, and arsenic treatment. Thus, our work identifies two types of Pol II displacement regions, which are differentially affected by perturbations of cellular homeostasis.

works.title: Inter-individual gene expression variability implies stable regulation of brain-biased genes across organs in three ray-finned fishes
works.abstract: Phenotypic variation among individuals provides the raw material for evolution, and gene expression is a key mediator between genetic and phenotypic variation. As for phenotypes, the range of gene expression is limited and biased by evolutionary and developmental constraints. Observed expression variability due to biomolecular stochasticity and cell-to-cell heterogeneity has been well-studied in isogenic populations of unicellular organisms. However, for multicellular organisms with a diversity of cells and tissues sharing the same genetic background, the interplay between expression variability, gene and organ function, and gene regulation remains an open question. Here, we use highly multiplexed 3'-end bulk RNA sequencing to generate transcriptome profiles spanning at least nine organs in outbred individuals of three ray-finned fish species: zebrafish, Northern pike, and spotted gar. Per organ, we quantify individual-to-individual gene expression variability independent of mean expression level. Lowly variable genes are enriched in cellular housekeeping functions whereas highly variable genes are enriched in stimulus-response functions. Furthermore, highly variable genes evolve under weaker purifying selection at the protein-coding sequence, indicating that intra-species expression variability predicts inter-species protein sequence divergence. Genes that are broadly expressed across organs are both highly expressed and lowly variable, whereas organ-biased genes are typically highly variable within their top organ. Among organ-biased genes, patterns of expression variance are dependent on the top organ. Specifically, brain- and gonads-biased genes have lowly variable expression across different organs, suggesting stabilizing selection. These patterns suggest that gene regulatory mechanisms evolve under organ-specific selective pressures.

works.title: Refining indel- and structural variant-trait associations with LAVrefiner
works.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are major sources of human genetic diversity. Despite advances in SV discovery, most single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-centric frameworks overlook sequence-level information and encode overlapping variants as independent features, potentially reducing power in association studies, biasing heritability estimation, and limiting prediction accuracy. Here, we present LAVrefiner, a scalable, sequence-aware method that decomposes overlapping sequence-resolved SVs and indels into nonoverlapping refined sequence components and generates genotype matrices compatible with standard SNP-based analyses. In tandem repeat (TR) regions, LAVrefiner further supports motif-aware allele comparison and repeat copy-number estimation. When applied to variants from the 1000 Genomes Project, LAVrefiner identifies 224,708 refined variants. Simulations show that LAVrefiner is fast and memory-efficient while maintaining robust genotype representations under TR-associated sequencing noise. In gene expression analyses, models combining LAVrefiner-derived copy-number estimates with refined variants yield the highest heritability estimates and prediction accuracy in short tandem repeat (STR) and variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) regions, outperforming models based on the original SV/indel representation and existing TR copy-number tools. Cis -expression quantitative trait locus ( cis -eQTL) mapping further shows that refined variants can localize regulatory signals to specific sequence components, including an independent VNTR-derived signal at the TFRC locus. Together, LAVrefiner provides an efficient, context-aware strategy for integrating sequence-resolved SVs and indels into existing genetic analysis frameworks.

works.title: ENflorA: a flexible tool for the bulk submission of next generation sequencing data to the European Nucleotide Archive
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: With the advancement of sequencing technologies and increasing quality of assembly and annotation tools, the amount of biological sequence data produced by research grows rapidly. To keep this data accessible for potential re-analysis, it is typically stored in public online databases, such as the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA). However, the increase in data entails an increase in time needed for metadata curation and upload. We propose a tool to simplify and automatize the upload of experimental and metadata to public repositories. RESULTS: We developed ENflorA, a set of scripts by which sample, sequence read and (annotated) assembly data can be uploaded to ENA in a simple and standardized manner. Our software allows easy metadata entry via spreadsheets, is suitable for batch upload of data from different sources, and can be fully integrated in bioinformatic workflows. It is platform independent and can be run natively on High Performance Computers, integrates an lftp upload option for big files and a test upload option. CONCLUSIONS: By easing the ENA submission process, ENflorA contributes to making high-throughput sequencing data findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable.

works.title: A new explainable AI pipeline for cancer cell segmentation and classification for microscopy images
works.abstract: Abstract Background The development of novel therapeutic approaches to cancers requires significant time and labour, especially for uncommon cancers (e.g. of mesenchymal origin). In addition, these rare cancers typically receive less research attention but still need sufficient analysis. For example, a trustworthy analysis of tissue samples to identify cancer progression and cell response to candidate therapies is a task to develop certain treatments and drugs. Thus, this research work develops a new explainable Deep Learning pipeline for accurate, high-throughput and autonomous recognition of metastasising cells from large-scale fluorescence microscopy images, which can be used to evaluate cell response with low cost and high trustworthiness, and facilitate the therapeutic approaches development. Results The pipeline includes pre-trained and domain-generalised segmentation to identify single cells, training the latest self-supervised transformers: DINO-based models to provide normal or metastasising classification, and leveraging Explainable AI methods to produce biologically meaningful model explanations towards the trustworthiness of model predictions; this is crucial in future clinical applications. Compared to supervised learning-based models, DINO achieves the best predictability (over 97% F1-weighted score) when only training the classifier, and the most efficient downstream adaptation. Besides, all DINO-based models can classify successfully when finetuning the entire model (DINOv3 achieves the highest F1-weighted score with 98.35%). We have also used an additional cross-magnification test and a self- / weakly-supervised model comparison to discuss the generalisation ability and superiority of DINO-based models. Biologically accurate model explanations are produced via heatmaps and analysed through quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluation; the important cell regions in the model decision-making process align well with biological consensus. We also demonstrate that biologically meaningful cytoskeletal features can be detected and exploited by the developed pipeline for cancer cell classification, which facilitates the development of cytoskeleton-based diagnosis. Conclusion We develop a precise, efficient, and trustworthy pipeline that can facilitate the development of effective and bespoke cancer treatments via AI-assisted testing of the response of cancer cells to various treatments and drugs.

works.title: HGACL-DRP: Heterogeneous graph attention dual-perturbation contrastive learning network for drug response prediction
works.abstract: The marked heterogeneity of cancer poses a substantial challenge to precision drug therapy, resulting in considerable variability in patient responses to identical treatments. Accurately predicting drug sensitivity thus represents an urgent and critical challenge in the field of pharmacology and personalized medicine. Existing methods have limitations in addressing the complexity of multi-modal biological data and heterogeneous graphs. Additionally, their heavy reliance on labeled data hinders model generalization. In this work, we propose the Heterogeneous Graph Attention Dual-Perturbation Contrastive Learning Network for Drug Response Prediction (HGACL-DRP). This framework constructs an optimized heterogeneous graph structure by integrating multi-omics features and implementing a robust neighbor filtering mechanism. HGACL-DRP innovatively introduces a Dual-Perturbation contrastive learning paradigm that incorporates both feature and structural perturbations specifically designed for drug response prediction, thereby enabling the self-supervised learning of more robust heterogeneous graph node embeddings. On two major public datasets, the Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC) and the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia (CCLE), HGACL-DRP exhibits exceptional performance across multiple classification metrics, achieving a mean AUC of 95.48% on CCLE and 98.99% on GDSC. Compared to existing state-of-the-art drug response prediction algorithms, HGACL-DRP demonstrates statistically significant improvements in predictive accuracy. The innovative multi-view graph augmentation strategy and attention mechanism are designed to enhance personalized drug selection and facilitate novel drug discovery. HGACL-DRP is anticipated to address the challenges posed by drug response heterogeneity, thereby providing reliable support for clinical decision-making. Not applicable.

works.title: Prompting alone is insufficient for large language model-based clinical variant classification
works.abstract: Accurate clinical genetic variant classification is becoming increasingly challenging as data volume and knowledge complexity increase. Large Language Models (LLMs) could potentially automate evidence retrieval and assist variant interpretation. To systematically evaluate the capacity of general-purpose LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity) to support clinical genetic variant classification. We analyzed 475 variants across 185 genes, with reference classifications established by expert variant scientists. Classification was performed by the four LLMs using a detailed structured prompting strategy and compared with a commercial non-LLM specialized platform. Performance was evaluated at the classification and criteria levels and stratified by various variant characteristics. Detailed prompting generally improved performance. Mean LLM classification concordance was 69.0% (70.2% precision and 68.2% recall), which was substantially lower than the 81.1% concordance (80.2% precision and 84.5% recall) achieved by the specialized commercial non-LLM platform tested. Concordance varied across variant types, with unadjusted mean concordance ranging from 87.2% for intronic variants to 56.0% for splice-region variants; adjusted associations were model-specific. At the criteria level, performance was highly criterion-specific: sensitivity exceeded 80% for BP7, PP3, PVS1, and PM2, but criterion-call precision and exact-strength agreement were substantially lower for several criteria. General-purpose LLMs used through direct or structured prompting demonstrated substantial limitations in clinical genetic variant classification compared with a specialized interpretation platform. These findings indicate that the common conversational approach of asking an LLM to classify a variant, even with detailed instructions, is insufficient for autonomous clinical use.

works.title: Interpretable Drug Response Prediction via Integrating Cellular Multi-Omics and Drug Structures
Leveraging genomic deep learning models for the prediction of noncoding variant effects
Genome-wide detection of genotype–environment interactions at biobank scale with fastGxE
works.abstract: Traditional genome-wide association studies have primarily focused on detecting main genotype effects, often overlooking genotype-environment interactions (GxE), which are essential for understanding context-specific genetic effects and refining disease etiology. Here we present fast genotype-environment interaction analysis (fastGxE), a scalable and effective genome-wide GxE method designed to identify genetic variants that interact with environmental factors to influence traits of interest. fastGxE controls for polygenic effects, polygenic interaction effects and noise heterogeneity; it remains robust to the number of environmental factors involved in GxE interactions; and it ensures scalability for genome-wide GxE analysis in large biobank studies, achieving speed improvements of 32.98-126.49 times over existing approaches. We illustrate the benefits of fastGxE through extensive simulations and an in-depth analysis of 32 physical traits and 67 blood biomarkers from the UK Biobank. In real-data applications, fastGxE identifies 7 genomic loci associated with physical traits, including 4 novel ones, and 18 genomic loci associated with blood biomarkers, 12 of which are novel. The new discoveries highlight the dynamic interplay between genetics and the environment, uncovering potentially clinically relevant pathways that could inform personalized interventions and treatment strategies.

works.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 60 loci associated with liver triglyceride content
works.abstract: Abstract We performed a large-scale genome-wide association study meta-analysis of magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver triglyceride content across 71,488 European-ancestry participants from the UK Biobank, approximately doubling the sample size of previous genome-wide association studies 1 . We identified 60 independent loci, including 31 not previously reported, and estimated the single nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability of liver triglyceride content at 25%. Integrative fine-mapping and gene-prioritization analyses nominated candidate effector genes for 48 loci. Of the 31 newly identified variants, 14 were validated in meta-analyses of clinically diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (42,163 cases and 1,646,254 controls). People in the highest versus lowest decile of a polygenic risk score for liver triglyceride content had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma. Plasma proteins associated with the liver triglyceride polygenic risk score were enriched for metabolic remodeling and inflammatory pathways, with liver-enriched protein signatures increasing and visceral adipose signatures decreasing with higher genetic risk. Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of liver triglyceride content, linking polygenic susceptibility to downstream metabolic and inflammatory pathways and providing insights into the genetic basis of steatotic liver disease.

works.title: The average individual genome: a survey of nearly 1 million whole-genome sequences
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: As whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly used in clinical and public health contexts, clearer expectations regarding the amount of variation present in the "average" human genome are required to contextualise findings. METHODS: We analysed WGS data from two large population cohorts: 490,541 individuals in UK Biobank (UKB) and 414,830 individuals in All of Us. Following variant and genotype QC, we aimed to assess the range of neutral and disease-associated variation across six genetically-inferred ancestry groups. RESULTS: The "average" genome contains ~4.3-5.3 million variants, of which ~1.5% are rare (within-cohort allele frequency < 1%). This includes ~67 autosomal deletions/duplications > 10,000 basepairs per genome, and rare autosomal copy number variants > 1 Mb present in ~ 1 in 41 (2.5%) individuals. On average, ~32-42% of variants per person are homozygous and individuals have ~4 unique runs of homozygosity > 1.5 Mb, with marked variation observed across ancestry groups. Of the ~21- 26,000 SNVs/indels per person in coding exons of MANE Select transcripts, ~48% are predicted to alter the protein, of which ~0.8% are high-confidence loss-of-function and ~0.1% have REVEL score > 0.7 suggestive of pathogenicity. Depending upon parental age, the average genome contains ~63 de novo variants, of which ~75-80% are paternal in origin. Considering only rare variants in GenCC-curated monogenic disease-associated genes, the average genome contains ~1-3 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, ~2-5 high-confidence loss-of-function variants, and ~50 ClinVar variants of uncertain significance. Most ClinVar pathogenic variants are heterozygous in recessive disease genes, consistent with carrier status, and have multiple ClinVar submitters. Finally, applying polygenic scores (PGS) for 28 common diseases within UKB, we estimate that the average person is in the top 10% for ~3 conditions, and around 1 in 5 people are in the top 1% for at least one PGS. CONCLUSIONS: The ubiquity of genetic variation in individuals has important implications for policy-makers considering genomic screening and clinicians counselling families. The continued underrepresentation of many global populations reflects a broader limitation of contemporary genomic research, underscoring the need for more inclusive datasets worldwide in order to enable equitable precision medicine.

works.title: Meta-analysis of over 8,000 individuals from Hawai‘i and Samoa for genetic associations to cardiometabolic phenotypes
authors: Lifestyle and Genetic Adaptations (OLaGA) Study Group The Samoan Obesity
Lifestyle and Genetic Adaptations (OLaGA) Study Group The Samoan Obesity
works.abstract: Although genome-wide association studies (GWAS) now routinely reveal genetic associations and biological insights in millions of individuals, underrepresentation of global populations, such as those from Polynesia, continue to persist. These exclusions, often driven by logistical challenges and lack of data, prevent systematic identification of population-enriched associations, such as the association of the missense variant at the CREBRF locus to BMI and type 2 diabetes discovered commonly occurring in Polynesian populations due to its rarity in global populations. Armed with the recently updated TOPMed imputation panel that could benefit studies in diverse populations that previously had poorer imputation performance, we performed the first GWAS of Native Hawaiians and Samoans, the largest to date of Polynesian-ancestry populations (combined N up to 8,461) to identify population-enriched associations for 13 adiposity and cardiometabolic traits available across both cohorts: BMI, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HDL, height, hip circumference, HOMA-IR, LDL, T2D, total cholesterol, triglycerides, waist circumference, and waist-hip ratio. We found 25 trait-loci associations that met genome-wide significance: 20 previously reported or known associations and 5 putatively new associations via meta-analysis. In particular, with improved statistical power, we were able to confirm the previously suggestive association between the missense CREBRF variant with fasting glucose levels. The remaining 4 potentially novel loci-trait associations for BMI, LDL, and waist-hip ratio, however, were not replicated in All-of-Us. The lack of Polynesian-enriched findings outside of the CREBRF locus informs the bounds of the effect sizes or frequencies of any enriched variants and suggests that further expansion of cohort sizes from this region of the world and improved imputation references specific to these populations are needed to identify more population-enriched associations.

works.title: The role of gene regulatory evolution in weapon diversification: Insights from comparative genomics, chromatin profiling, and functional analyses of BMP signaling in horned beetles
works.abstract: Condition-responsive growth is a common feature of multicellular development, during which organisms integrate genetic and environmental signals to adjust their phenotype. However, the molecular properties shaping condition-responsive diversification remain poorly understood. The beetle genus Onthophagus offers promising opportunities to investigate this question, given its diversity of sex- and nutrition-responsive phenotypes, including horns - novel, secondary sexual weapons used in reproductive competition. We compared the gene regulatory properties of horns in two closely related species exhibiting highly specialized sex- and nutrition-biased phenotypes. We found a dynamic cis-regulatory landscape in developing horn tissue, shaped by mutational accumulation across species, condition-specific changes in chromatin accessibility within species, and the acquisition of lineage-specific regulatory elements. Many of these putative regulatory regions include binding site motifs of critical developmental regulatory genes, including members of the bone morphogenetic protein signaling pathway. We provide functional evidence that two proteins in this pathway have been co-opted for horn development, influencing the shape and size of this trait across species, sexes, and nutritional states. These findings provide evidence that evolutionarily labile cis-regulatory interactions may evolve alongside diversification of condition-specific traits, potentially modifying the activity of conserved developmental pathways over short evolutionary timescales.

works.title: Distilling Direct Effects via Conditional Differential Gene Expression Analysis
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: Differential gene expression (DGE) analysis is foundational for interpreting RNA sequencing data, but it conflates direct biological effects with correlations propagated through gene co-expression. Across three RNA sequencing datasets (including a genome-scale perturb-seq experiment), we find that only a small fraction of differentially expressed genes have direct effects on the trait of interest, while the majority are undirected or passengers whose associations are mediated through other genes. RESULTS: To distinguish direct effect genes, we introduce conditional differential gene expression (CDGE) analysis, a framework that tests for conditional rather than marginal association between each gene and the trait of interest. Implemented via the GhostKnockoff procedure with lasso regression, CDGE delivers false discovery rate control, operates on summary statistics from existing DGE pipelines, and accommodates batch effects. The genes identified by CDGE mediate the effects of most other differentially expressed genes and show stronger enrichment for known protein-protein interactions and biological pathways than DGE-identified genes. These results suggest that the field has been systematically over-interpreting DGE outputs, and that distinguishing direct from mediated effects is essential for prioritizing genes for functional follow-up and therapeutic development. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: To facilitate public access to knockoff-based CDGE analysis, we have developed the R package "KnockoffCDGE" as an integrated implementation, which is freely available at https://github.com/GuJQ5/KnockoffCDGE (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23241517).

works.title: MSCquartets 3.3: Fast Inference of Species Networks and Trees of Blobs under the Multispecies Coalescent
works.abstract: The R package MSCquartets offers a suite of methods for testing and inferring species relationships from gene trees under coalescent models. MSCquartets 3.3 significantly extends the functionality of version 1.0 by implementing the TINNiK and ECToBlob algorithms for inference of the tree of blobs under the network multispecies coalescent model (NMSC). Additionally, it implements the NANUQ+ algorithm, a fast method for inference of level-1 networks. Computational speed of all functionalities is greatly improved through use of C ++ routines, and a Shiny App is introduced for easier exploration of basic analyses. Availability and implementation: MSCquartets 3.3 is available on the Comprehensive R Archive Network, at https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=MSCquartets. The MSCquartets 3.3 Shiny App is available at https://mscquartets.shinyapps.io/MSCq-app/.

works.title: Integrating complementary datasets for constructing microbiome–metabolome–disease pathways
works.abstract: MOTIVATION: Microbiome-metabolome-disease pathways play a central role in host health, but studying them is limited by the data available. Large clinical microbiome cohorts often lack metabolomic measurements, while multi-omics studies with paired profiles are typically small or incompletely phenotyped. Combining such complementary datasets is challenging: the metabolite is not measured in the clinical cohort, microbiome data are high-dimensional and compositional, and log-ratio analyses depend on an arbitrarily chosen reference taxon. RESULTS: We propose a framework that integrates a large target cohort that has microbiome and outcome data with a smaller external study that has paired microbiome-metabolome profiles. A high-dimensional structural equation model jointly links the microbiome, the metabolome, and the disease outcome. It allows for unmeasured confounding and groups microbes into functional categories. We address compositionality with the additive log-ratio (ALR) transformation, estimate parameters by penalized two-stage least squares, and test metabolite-disease associations with a regularized permutation test. A novel multiple-reference procedure treats each microbe in turn as the ALR reference. It combines the resulting P-values with the Cauchy combination test and classifies microbes by stability selection, which makes inference robust to the choice of reference. In simulations, the method controls the type I error rate, and its power increases with both target and external sample sizes. An application to inflammatory bowel disease, integrating the FRAN and iHMP cohorts, reveals biologically interpretable microbiome-metabolome-disease links. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The method is implemented in the R package MMDP, freely available at https://github.com/lei-fang-stat/MMDP.

works.title: A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection
works.abstract: Accurate detection of Z-DNA-forming regions is limited by the trade-off between sensitivity and specificity in sequence-based methods. We present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0-a fast and interpretable protocol that extends Z-DNA Hunter through a dual-scan strategy combined with a fuzzy expert layer. A permissive scan (model 2, minimum length 6 bp, threshold 30%) captures a broad candidate set, while a stringent scan (model 2, minimum length 10 bp, threshold 60%) provides high-confidence support. These outputs are integrated using fuzzy inference incorporating sequence signal, cross-scan support, genomic context, and bias penalties. On the audited 385-locus Shin analysis, the protocol achieves balanced accuracy 0.883 (recall 0.862, specificity 0.904), comparable with the published Z-DNABERT operating point, while alternative modes increase specificity to 0.973. The paired scans are combined by a transparent, configurable prioritization layer with an adjustable recall-specificity trade-off. The local workflow requires only a FASTA (Fast-All sequence alignment format), sequence and transcription start site annotation. The tool is freely available at https://github.com/mifo123/zdna-fuzzy-hunter.

works.title: MineGraph facilitates plastid and mitochondrial graph pangenome analysis in plants
works.abstract: The rapid growth of genomic sequencing is driving the implementation of graph pangenomes in evolutionary studies, yet the computational costs and complex interpretations at higher taxonomic levels hinder their broad use. Here, we present an evolutionary graph pangenome (evograph) pipeline to streamline diversity analyses across species and families. Applying this framework to 709 Poales chloroplast genomes indicates that genomic diversity is driven primarily by species-specific variation. We resolve a 77.7 Kbp consensus genome and apply graph theory metrics to highlight distinct genus-level evolutionary signatures. Evographs provide a powerful, nuanced framework for resolving evolutionary complexity across high taxonomic levels.

works.title: PROBE: a multi-organism benchmark for evaluating general-purpose large language models on Gene Ontology protein function annotation
works.abstract: One of the most important unresolved issues in computational biology is systematic protein function annotation. Despite decades of curation by the Gene Ontology Consortium and UniProt Swiss-Prot, most sequenced proteins lack experimentally validated functional annotations. The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) trained on scientific literature raises the question of whether they can map natural-language descriptions of experimentally characterized protein function to the correct Gene Ontology (GO) terms without task-specific training. Answering this question requires a benchmark with gold-standard experimental annotations and multi-organism coverage, which existing benchmarks lack. We introduce PROBE ( PR otein functi O n B enchmark E valuation): 1,000 UniProt Swiss-Prot proteins from five organisms, experimental-evidence-only annotations. We evaluate 10 open-source LLMs across five prompt formats, zero-shot and inference-only, yielding 150,000 predictions. The best model (Mistral Large 123B) achieves macro-F1 of 9.3%, yet a most-frequent-5 heuristic outperforms four of the ten LLMs. 41.3% of predicted GO terms were unmatched to the benchmark’s annotations; a temporal-holdout check against current UniProt records found only 1.25% newly supported, suggesting most are genuine errors rather than incomplete ground truth. Performance varied by organism— Saccharomyces cerevisiae unexpectedly scored highest (F1 = 8.6%), but with only five organisms this does not track evolutionary distance, and neither literature density nor annotation-pool size reaches significance, so the finding remains exploratory. Candidate-selection prompting (P5) reduces the unmatched-prediction rate by 33.5 percentage points relative to P1 while achieving the highest F1 (8.2%). GO semantic similarity analysis shows LLM predictions exceed a random baseline by 2.1–2.6× across all namespaces, indicating biologically meaningful semantic alignment despite exact-match failures. A preliminary 50-protein comparison of four closed-source models against the best open-source model found F1 of 0.081–0.127 versus 0.099 (0.028-point gap), suggesting but not establishing that current limitations extend beyond open-source models. PROBE shows that general-purpose LLMs can map some natural-language descriptions of protein function to GO terms, but performance is often insufficient and unreliable for autonomous annotation. Unmatched predictions are common, and organism-level performance differences remain an open question rather than explained by training data or evolutionary relationships. The benchmark, evaluation pipeline, and all 150,000 experimental response records are publicly available to ensure reproducibility.

works.title: Genomic in vitro transcription and Nanopore direct RNA sequencing of a human B-Lymphocyte cell line
works.abstract: Genomic DNA used as a template for in vitro transcription of RNA can serve as a true negative control for benchmarking RNA modification detection by Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) models. We generated DRS data for in vitro transcribed (IVT) RNA composed of canonical nucleotides using genomic DNA from a human cell line. We applied Dorado modification calling models to these data, and calculated 9-mer specific false-positive rates for eight RNA modifications as a comparison point for future development of RNA modification models.

works.title: Spatial Multi-Omics Integration with Mass Spectrometry Imaging: Decoding Metabolic Landscapes and Disease Mechanisms
GlycoAudit: structural joinability and annotation degree shape glycan–agent relation ranking
works.abstract: Abstract Motivation Benchmark scores can be misleading when identifier resolution, structural availability, and incomplete interaction annotation determine which glycans can be evaluated. GlycoAudit audits this evidence-to-structure path before model comparison. Results A strict accession, branch, and sequence contract retained 44 of 173 resolved SugarBind glycans (25.4%) and excluded 129 (74.6%). The joined domain was substantially more densely annotated. Under leakage-controlled held-out-positive ranking, the Web3 Unique Representation of Carbohydrate Structures (WURCS) exceeded the evaluated global structural summaries. Yet a leave-one-agent-out annotation-degree control achieved higher mean reciprocal rank (0.491 versus 0.381) and higher known-positive average precision (APknown), 0.489 versus 0.373, whereas WURCS achieved higher Recall@5 (0.688 versus 0.456). These metric-dependent reversals show that structural joinability, annotation degree, candidate construction, and evaluation choice jointly shape apparent benchmark performance. The release evaluates positive-relation ranking, not confirmed non-binding classification or cross-source transfer. Availability GlycoAudit makes evidence, joining decisions, exclusions, candidates, folds, controls, and machine-readable results inspectable in the public GlycoAudit repository.

works.title: Multiancestry conditional and joint analysis applied to GWAS summary statistics
works.abstract: Conditional and joint (COJO) analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) data is a standard post-GWAS analysis for identifying statistically independent associations. Although GWAS meta-analyses are increasingly conducted across multiple ancestry groups, the optimal strategy for multiancestry COJO analysis remains unclear. Here we introduce Manc-COJO, a method for multiancestry COJO analysis. Simulations and real-data analyses show that Manc-COJO improves detection of independent association signals while reducing false positives compared with single-ancestry COJO implemented in genome-wide complex trait analysis (GCTA) and its ad-hoc multiancestry adaptations. We also introduce Manc-COJO:FIX, a follow-up algorithm to identify ancestry-specific independent associations. The C++ implementation of Manc-COJO is over 120-fold faster than GCTA-COJO and supports linkage disequilibrium references derived from either individual-level genotype data or pre-computed matrices, facilitating analyses when data sharing is limited.

works.title: A systems perspective on monoallelic inborn errors of immunity
Imputation of fluid intelligence to increase power for gene discovery
The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree informs on gene essentiality
works.abstract: Abstract Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into gene essentiality under natural selection.
